title: Digital ambition under ecological constraints: Governing AI in climate-vulnerable South Africa
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is promoted as a driver of development and sustainability. However, its deployment remains embedded in energy-, water-, material-, and land-intensive infrastructures operating under significant ecological and resource constraints. Drawing on environmental policy integration, sustainability transitions, socio-metabolic theory, and socio-ecological-technical systems (SETS) research, the study examines the extent to which environmental considerations are integrated into AI governance. Using qualitative comparative policy analysis, complemented by contextual documentary evidence on South Africa's emerging digital infrastructure, the study identifies a structural governance gap: AI policy has evolved largely in parallel with environmental and infrastructure governance systems. This misalignment limits the state's capacity to anticipate resource pressures, manage infrastructural lock-in, and steer AI deployment toward sustainable trajectories. Rather than proposing new regulatory regimes, the article advances a transition-oriented Green AI governance framework that leverages existing mechanisms for environmental screening and authorisation, sustainable public procurement, infrastructure and resource-capacity planning, resource transparency and disclosure, and institutional coordination. The South African case highlights a broader challenge facing climate-vulnerable contexts, where digital transformation risks outpacing governance capacity. The findings contribute to sustainability transitions scholarship by demonstrating how emerging digital technologies can be incrementally embedded within existing governance systems to align innovation with biophysical limits.

title: ENSURING CYBERSECURITY IN THE CONTEXT OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION: A RISK-BASED MANAGEMENT AND RESILIENCE MODEL
summary: igital transformation expands access to government, financial, educational, and commercial services, but at the same time increases organizations’ dependence on information systems, network services, cloud platforms, and external providers. Under these conditions, cybersecurity should be viewed not merely as a set of technical safeguards, but as a system of continuous risk management that ensures data confidentiality, integrity, and availability; process resilience; the protection of data subjects’ rights; and business recovery following incidents. The purpose of this article is to systematize the main threats and cybersecurity measures, compare international statistical indicators, and propose a multi-level practical model for commercial organizations and government agencies. This study is based on an analysis of documents from the International Telecommunication Union and the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity, as well as reports from Verizon and IBM, and on a comparative and systematic analysis of approaches to cyber threat management. The data indicate that system vulnerabilities, ransomware, third-party risks, and the human factor remain key elements of the threat landscape. At the same time, the published metrics were obtained using various methodologies and cannot serve as a unified assessment of the frequency of global attacks. The article presents a model that integrates management, prevention, detection, response, and recovery. It was concluded that effective cybersecurity requires clearly measurable goals, the allocation of responsibilities, the protection of supply chains, regular practical exercises, and respect for privacy and other human rights. title: Strategic financing and sustainability decisions in dual-channel supply chains under demand uncertainty: a distribution-free game-theoretic perspective
summary: Purpose This study investigates how financing structure and sustainability investment jointly influence pricing, service, and green decision-making in a dual-channel supply chain under demand uncertainty. It particularly examines how bank financing and trade credit shape firms' ability to improve environmental performance, strengthen channel competitiveness, and enhance customer value. Design/methodology/approach A Stackelberg game-theoretic model is developed involving a manufacturer and a retailer who operate through both online and offline channels. The manufacturer invests in green innovation financed through bank borrowing, while the retailer chooses between bank financing with a wholesale price discount or trade credit with deferred payment. Demand is uncertain and influenced by green investment and retail service. A distribution-free approach is employed to derive robust equilibrium strategies without assuming a specific demand distribution. Findings Results show that financing choices critically shape sustainability-oriented decisions and channel coordination. Trade credit encourages higher green investment and retail service when financing costs are high, whereas bank financing is more effective under lower borrowing rates and stronger discount incentives. Demand uncertainty substantially affects inventory and profitability, particularly under high-variance settings. The distribution-free framework enhances decision robustness under uncertain market environments. Originality/value This study develops an integrated dual-channel supply chain framework combining green innovation, retail service, dual financing, and distribution-free demand modeling within a single analytical structure. It contributes to marketing intelligence by illustrating how financial structures and uncertainty jointly drive sustainable strategy formation and channel coordination. The findings provide actionable insights for managers seeking to align green innovation, retail service, and financing decisions to build competitive and sustainable supply chains.

title: Green Finance Business Model Innovation in Indonesian State-Owned Banks toward Net Zero Emission 2060: A Triple Layered Business Model Canvas Approach
summary: Purpose—This study examines how Indonesian state-owned banks organize economic, environmental, and social value creation through green finance in the context of Indonesia’s Net Zero Emissions (NZE) 2060 agenda. Method—A qualitative multiple-case study investigated Bank Rakyat Indonesia (BRI), Bank Mandiri, Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI), and Bank Tabungan Negara (BTN). Eight purposively selected informants, two per bank, were interviewed. Sustainability reports identified in the source manuscript as 2024 reports and institutional documents supplemented the interviews. Framework Analysis used the 27 components of the Triple Layered Business Model Canvas (TLBMC), with NVivo supporting data organization and cross-case comparison. Findings—The accounts indicate different emphases: inclusive micro, small, and medium enterprise financing at BRI; corporate and infrastructure financing at Mandiri; ESG governance at BNI; and housing finance at BTN. Sustainability commitments coexist with reported gaps in impact measurement and strategic–operational alignment. These patterns describe business orientations rather than a validated ranking of sustainability maturity. Conclusion and Implications—Green finance integration remains uneven. Banks should strengthen outcome measurement, organizational capabilities, and alignment across the three value layers. The findings identify potential support for the NZE agenda; they do not establish attributable emissions reductions or achievement of the national target. Originality/Value—The study adapts TLBMC to compare four banking cases and proposes an untested integration framework linking economic, environmental, and social value through governance and digital transformation. Purpose—This study examines how Indonesian state-owned banks organize economic, environmental, and social value creation through green finance in the context of Indonesia’s Net Zero Emissions (NZE) 2060 agenda.

Abstract. This article examines the statistical assessment of the mismatch between demand and supply in the labor market under the conditions of the digital economy. The study analyzes structural changes in labor market demand and supply, the growing need for digital competencies, and the differences between graduates’ qualifications and employers’ requirements. To identify labor market imbalances, the study proposes the use of statistical indicators such as the demand–supply coefficient, mismatch index, employment rate, average time to employment, and labor income. In addition, methodological approaches are substantiated for assessing the impact of digital competencies on labor market demand and forecasting future workforce requirements. The findings of the study have practical significance for aligning the volume of workforce training in different educational fields with labor market needs, developing digital competencies, and improving the efficiency of state-funded workforce planning. title: THE ROLE OF ELECTRONIC MARKETING IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE TOURISM INDUSTRY
summary: In the era of digital transformation, electronic marketing has become a crucial tool for the growth and competitiveness of the tourism industry. This article explores the role of e-marketing in enhancing tourism businesses, improving customer engagement, and expanding global reach. It examines various electronic marketing channels, including websites, social media, search engine optimization (SEO), email marketing, and online travel agencies (OTAs). The study analyzes how digital strategies influence tourist behavior, brand loyalty, and destination competitiveness. Through a comprehensive literature review and case studies, the research highlights the benefits, challenges, and future trends of electronic marketing in tourism. The findings suggest that effective e-marketing strategies significantly contribute to the sustainable development of tourism by fostering innovation, customer satisfaction, and business growth.

title: DEVELOPING A SYSTEMS THEORY OF SCIENTIFIC AND TECHNOLOGICAL HOMOGENEITY IN GASTRONOMY: STRUCTURE, PROCESS, AND INNOVATION IN FUTURE FOOD ECOSYSTEMS
summary: This conceptual paper aims to design a systems theory of scientific and technological homogeneity in gastronomy by demonstrating how systems thinking can be applied to food science, gastronomic innovation, and technology management to create a unified whole that fosters innovation, sustainability, and future food ecosystem resilience. This study employs a conceptual research design that achieves its objectives by conducting a systematic review of the existing literature on gastronomy, systems theory, food science, managing innovation, digital transformation, and sustainability to establish theoretical foundations for scientific and technological homogeneity. The review identifies relevant systems theory concepts that can be leveraged to unify diverse fields of food science while actualising scientific theories related to future food ecosystem management. As a result, this paper proposes a systems theory that integrates key components, processes, and functions that promote scientific and technological homogeneity in gastronomy. This study actualises how knowledge, technology, gastronomic techniques, and ecosystems can be unified to achieve homogeneity in scientific and technological processes. The paper argues that scientific and technological homogeneity is actualised through a convergence of structural, process, and innovation-related aspects. This paper shows that technological and scientific homogeneity in gastronomy can be achieved by understanding and leveraging the key components that contribute to standardised scientific knowledge, technical expertise, institutional infrastructure, and collaborative networks in the field. The study actualises process homogeneity by describing processes such as knowledge unification, digital transformation, quality assurance, decision-making analytics, and continuous learning that facilitate standardised gastronomic procedures. This paper demonstrates that innovation homogeneity is realised through articulating the relevant processes that promote standardised, consistent, and continual development of culinary innovations that improve the quality, safety, and sustainability of food products, services, and ecosystems. This study concludes by arguing that systems theory is critical in sensitising various stakeholders on the need for coherence in structures, processes, and systems to enhance future food ecosystem performance. This study makes a theoretical contribution to the existing body of knowledge by designing a systems theory of scientific and technological homogeneity in gastronomy that has not been emphasised in the previous research literature. The paper provides conceptual foundations for future process improvement, theoretical development, and policy studies in food science and technology, managing innovation, and sustainability.

title: Green Innovation Practices and Organizational Performance
summary: Green innovation has emerged as a critical pathway for firms seeking to reconcile environmental responsibility with competitive performance. While a growing body of research examines the relationship between green innovation and organizational outcomes, the literature remains fragmented, particularly with respect to emerging economies. This paper critically reviews the conceptual foundations, theoretical perspectives, and empirical evidence on green innovation practices and organizational performance. It synthesizes research across developed and developing contexts, with particular attention to the limited but expanding body of work from Nigeria and Africa. The review identifies four key dimensions of green innovation practices: green management practices, green process adherence, green product offering, and green marketing adoption; and evaluates their individual and joint effects on performance. Major gaps are highlighted in theoretical integration, contextual coverage, methodological approaches, and the operationalization of green innovation constructs. The paper concludes by proposing an integrated conceptual framework and a research agenda to guide future empirical investigations, especially in emerging market settings where institutional pressures and resource constraints shape the green innovation performance relationship differently from developed economies.

title: EVOLUTION OF FREDERICK TAYLOR’S MANAGEMENT IDEAS IN THE CONTEXT OF THE DIGITAL ECONOMY
summary: This study examines the evolution of Frederick Taylor’s management ideas in the context of the digital economy. It justifies the relevance of the topic in light of the ongoing processes driven by digitalization, automation, and the widespread adoption of information technologies in organizational activities. The paper reviews the main tenets of the scientific management concept and assesses their significance for the development of modern management science. The main principles of Taylorism, in particular the division of labor, standardization, work-rate setting, and control, are analyzed. It is established that these principles formed the basis for the development of effective models of labor organization in the industrial era and remain relevant in modern conditions. It is determined that in the digital economy, these principles are undergoing a transformation through their adaptation to new technological capabilities. The features of digital Taylorism as a contemporary stage in the development of scientific management are examined. It is demonstrated that digital tools serve as a modern form of implementing the classical principles of control, standardization, and planning. A comparative analysis of the classical and digital Taylorism has been conducted. It has been determined that modern approaches to management are characterized by a transition from rigidly regulated models to flexible, adaptive systems focused on the use of knowledge, innovation, and teamwork. A shift in the employee’s role has been identified – from an executor to a knowledge carrier and active participant in management processes. The advantages and risks of digital Taylorism have been identified. It has been demonstrated that, alongside improvements in management efficiency, labor productivity, and process transparency, digitalization can lead to increased control, reduced employee autonomy, formalization of their behavior, and an increase in psychological stress. The necessity of combining the principles of scientific management with a human-centered approach has been substantiated. The obtained results can be used in the development of modern human resource management systems, the formulation of digital transformation strategies for organizations, and the improvement of the approaches to evaluating work performance. The prospects for further research are related to studying the impact of digital technologies on organizational behavior, employee motivation, and the development of new management models in the context of the digital economy.

title: IMPROVING THE ORGANIZATIONAL FRAMEWORK OF ACCOUNTING AND ANALYTICAL SUPPORT IN THE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM OF FORESTRY ENTERPRISES
summary: The article examines the theoretical, methodological, and practical aspects of improving the organizational framework of accounting and analytical support in the management system of forestry enterprises under the conditions of digital transformation and sustainable development. It is substantiated that current challenges facing the forestry sector require the integration of financial, management, statistical, and environmental accounting into a unified information environment capable of generating reliable, relevant, and timely information for managerial decision-making. The study identifies the main causes of inconsistencies between accounting, management, and statistical reporting data, including inconsistencies in regulatory and methodological support, the use of heterogeneous software systems, differences in product classification, time discrepancies in data processing, and continuous legislative changes. The paper proposes the adaptation of the National Accounting Standard (NAS) 30 Biological Assets to the specific features of forestry activities through the clarification of terminology, improvement of biological asset and finished product valuation approaches, expansion of disclosure requirements in financial reporting, and refinement of forestry product classification. A theoretical and methodological framework for accounting representation of finished forestry products is developed, encompassing product classification, improved analytical accounting, enhanced documentation procedures, and the integration of economic, environmental, and social dimensions of forestry activities. Particular attention is devoted to the implementation of modern digital technologies, including ERP systems, electronic timber accounting, geographic information systems (GIS), Business Intelligence tools, artificial intelligence, and cloud technologies as key instruments for increasing transparency, efficiency, and responsiveness of management processes. The proposed recommendations contribute to improving the quality of accounting and analytical support, harmonizing national accounting practices with international standards, strengthening the reliability of financial reporting, and enhancing the competitiveness and sustainable development of forestry enterprises in the context of digital transformation.

title: Digital Accounting System to Improve Financial Transparency in An Employee Cooperative
summary: Originality/novelty: This study demonstrates how combining an accessible, low-cost digital tool (Google Sheets) with a member-facing WhatsApp distribution routine can effectively bridge the financial transparency gap and mitigate information asymmetry in small cooperatives. Objective: To evaluate the implementation of a low-cost digital accounting information system designed to replace manual handwritten records and restore member trust in an employee cooperative's governance. . Methods/approach: Framed as participatory action research with asset-based elements, the project spanned three phases: needs assessment, system design/implementation, and training/mentoring. Analyzed through the lens of TAM, digital transformation, and cooperative governance theory, data were gathered from four informants, observations, document analysis, and post-training questionnaires, evaluated using thematic analysis and triangulation. Results: Within four weeks, monthly financial reports became readily available to all board members. Post-training evaluations showed that 92% of respondents understood how to operate the system, while 85% expressed increased confidence in the cooperative’s financial transparency, promoting active member participation during meetings. Implications: The study highlights that small-scale cooperatives can achieve meaningful digital transformation and stronger governance without high financial investment, provided design simplicity, practical capacity building, and regular disclosure routines are prioritized.

title: Factors affecting the digital competence of workers in Vietnam coal enterprises
summary: This study focuses on analyzing the factors influencing the digital competence of workers in Vietnamese coal mining enterprises in the context of digital transformation increasingly impacting mining, processing, management, and labor organization. Based on a theoretical overview and related research, the article identifies five groups of factors that can affect the digital competence of workers: digital skills training and development; infrastructure and technological readiness; organizational support; individual learning orientation; and the degree of job digitization. The research results show that the digital competence of workers depends not only on their ability to access and use technology but is also significantly influenced by the learning environment, enterprise support, and the degree of integration of digital technology into daily work. Among these, training, self-learning ability, and organizational orientation play a crucial role in helping workers adapt to new job requirements. This research contributes to clarifying the mechanisms of digital competency formation within the context of coal industry enterprises, while also proposing several management implications to improve the training system, enhance access to technology, build a continuous learning environment, and promote the digitalization of work in conjunction with human resource development.

title: Exploring the role of sustainable finance in enhancing operational efficiency: evidence from firms listed on the London Stock Exchange
summary: Abstract Sustainable finance improves operational efficiency by directing capital toward environmentally responsible investments that reduce costs, optimize resource use, and enhance long-term productivity, while supporting firms’ transition toward greener, more efficient operations. This study applied the Resource-Based View (RBV) theory to examine how sustainable finance practices influence operational efficiency. It utilizes 17 years of data (2007–2023) from 143 non-financial companies, sourced from Thomson Reuters Eikon DataStream. To address endogeneity in the dataset, the study employs the Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) estimation model. Findings indicate that green bond issuance, environmental expenditures, emission reduction policies, and environmental investment initiatives have a significant impact on operational efficiency. Additionally, the interaction between green bond issuance and firm size significantly influences operational efficiency. These results suggest that corporations should prioritize green financing and environmentally sustainable strategies, while carefully assessing the cost-effectiveness of environmental expenditures. Aligning green initiatives with firm size can further enhance operational efficiency and support long-term environmental and performance objectives.

title: A Multi-State Linear Influence Model for Cyber Risk Propagation in Supply Chains
summary: Modern multi-echelon supply chains of critical infrastructure are increasingly defined by hyper-connectivity, driven by software integrations, cloud-based architectures, and enterprise resource planning synchronization. While these digital integrations optimize operational throughput, they simultaneously expose industrial networks to systemic, cascading cyber risks. Traditional supply chain risk management paradigms are often inadequate to capture the time-varying, multi-stage degradation characteristics of cyber threat propagation through the chain. This article introduces a baseline cyber risk propagation framework that couples a linear influence model (LIM) paradigm with a discrete 4-state operational security condition: Secure, Vulnerable, Compromised, and Offline. The proposed architecture leverages the additive and time-decaying properties of LIM frameworks to inherently resolve cyclic operational feedback loops while bypassing exponential state-space explosion. To operationalize the mathematical framework, we investigate four core resilience metrics: time-to-impact, area under the curve, cyber bullwhip effect, and recovery lag. Numerical simulations demonstrate the feasibility of this computationally tractable framework on synthetic networks, illustrating how it can be used to audit cascading propagation, evaluate containment strategies, and compare mitigation policies across multi-echelon ecosystems.

title: An Analysis of Tesla's Supply Chain Management Model
summary: As the global new energy vehicle (NEV) industry enters a phase of stock competition and high-quality development, supply chain management capabilities, cost optimization levels, and resilience to supply chain risks have become key sources of competitive differentiation among automakers, fundamentally changing the traditional automotive industry's emphasis on scale-based competition. Tesla, as a benchmark enterprise in the global NEV industry, has established a new supply chain management system that is underpinned by digitalization, features vertical integration as its core barrier, and integrates global layout with localized adaptation and coordination. The model also incorporates multiple supply sources and production locations to diversify supply chain risks. This paper takes Tesla's supply chain management model as the research object, systematically analyzing its core supply chain characteristics from three major frameworks: upstream supplier layout, midstream independent manufacturing of core technologies, and downstream direct-to-consumer (D2C) services. Additionally, it examines the practical challenges faced by Tesla's supply chain in the context of current global geopolitical conflicts, overseas policy barriers, and fluctuations in mineral resources. The study finds that the core advantages of Tesla's supply chain model lie in eliminating information silos across the entire chain through digital technology, gaining control over costs and technology through independent research and production in core areas, and achieving cost reduction, efficiency improvement, and risk diversification through a globally dispersed layout and deep localization adaptation. However, the model also has limitations, including limited resilience to supply disruptions resulting from a streamlined supplier base and substantial exposure to foreign-market policy changes.

summary: The digital transformation occurring within Islamic educational institutions requires a more adaptive and professional management system capable of meeting the demands for efficiency, accountability, and quality improvement. This study aims to analyze the implementation of fundamental Islamic educational management functions (POAC: Planning, Organizing, Actuating, Controlling) within a technology-based management system at Al-Ma'soem Islamic Boarding School, as well as to identify the challenges and opportunities emerging from this digitalization process. Employing a qualitative field-study design, data were collected through in-depth interviews, limited observations, and document analysis related to the digital management system. The findings indicate that planning, organizing, actuating, and controlling have been integrated through the use of management information systems, digital-competence-based staff recruitment, the utilization of digital administrative and learning applications, and monitoring mechanisms supported by dashboards and content-filtering systems. The results confirm that digitalization enhances the effectiveness of pesantren governance, although its success depends heavily on human resource readiness, infrastructure stability, and an organizational culture supportive of innovation. Theoretically, this study expands the discourse on Islamic educational management by offering the POAC-Digital concept, which integrates technological adaptation with Islamic values. Practically, the findings provide a strategic reference for developing modern pesantren management models that are more effective, accountable, and quality-oriented.

title: Impact of artificial intelligence on project planning, scheduling, and control
summary: Abstract The growing complexity of engineering and construction projects has revealed the weaknesses of conventional project planning, scheduling, and control approaches. Traditional tools often employ fixed assumptions, deterministic models, and past averages, which are inadequate for dealing with uncertainty, dynamic environments, and large-scale data. Artificial intelligence has become a disruptive technology that can be used to improve decision-making, prediction, and automation in project management processes. This paper examines the application of artificial intelligence in project planning, scheduling, and control within the engineering and construction sector. The paper summarises the application of artificial intelligence methods, including machine learning, optimization algorithms, and predictive analytics, in enhancing project performance using a methodical review of the recent scholarly literature and industry practise. The results show that artificial intelligence promotes the planning accuracy, flexibility of scheduling, and real-time project control to a great extent, as it allows data-driven insights and flexible responses. Issues of data quality, company preparedness, and ethical issues are major obstacles to implementation. The research paper adds to the project management literature because it develops the application of artificial intelligence in the three fundamental project management functions and provides practical advice to practitioners interested in introducing intelligent project management systems. title: HALFWAY TO 2015-2030 SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALS: HOW HAS THE JOURNEY FARED SO FAR IN NIGERIA?
summary: The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), adopted by the United Nations in 2015, provide a global framework for promoting inclusive economic growth, social equity, and environmental sustainability by 2030. As the implementation period reaches its midpoint, concerns have intensified regarding the likelihood of achieving the SDG targets, particularly in developing countries such as Nigeria. This study assesses progress toward the SDGs between 2015 and 2025, with emphasis on Africa and Nigeria, and evaluates Nigeria's prospects for attaining the 2030 targets. A qualitative review methodology was employed, relying exclusively on secondary data from peer-reviewed journal articles, policy documents, and reports published by the United Nations, World Bank, African Development Bank, National Bureau of Statistics, OSSAP-SDGs, WHO, UNESCO, FAO, and other reputable institutions. The findings indicate that Nigeria has made notable progress in institutionalizing the SDGs, expanding infrastructure, improving renewable energy access, advancing digital transformation, and strengthening development partnerships, with relatively stronger performance in SDGs 7, 9, 11, and 17. However, progress remains uneven, as poverty, food insecurity, inadequate healthcare, educational deficits, gender inequality, weak institutions, insecurity, climate change, and financing constraints continue to impede achievement of several goals. The study concludes that Nigeria is unlikely to achieve all 17 SDGs by 2030 under the current trajectory but can make substantial progress through strengthened governance, increased investment in human capital and infrastructure, improved data systems, climate-resilient policies, and enhanced multi-stakeholder partnerships

title: Protecting Workers' Right to Mental Health in Digital Work Environments: Legal Challenges and Reform Directions in Vietnam
summary: Digital work technologies increasingly determine when, how, and at what intensity work is performed. Continuous connectivity, electronic monitoring, algorithmic management, and technology-enabled harassment can generate psychosocial risks that are not adequately addressed by legal rules designed mainly for physical workplaces. This article asks whether Vietnamese labour and occupational safety and health law provides a coherent preventive framework for protecting workers’ mental health in digital work environments and which comparative models can guide reform. It uses doctrinal analysis, interdisciplinary literature synthesis, and functional comparison with international standards and selected approaches in the European Union, France, and Australia. The analysis finds that Vietnamese law contains relevant constitutional, working-time, occupational safety and health, dignity, anti-harassment, and personal-data safeguards, but these rules remain fragmented. In particular, psychosocial risks are not expressly defined or systematically assessed; workers have no statutory right to disconnect; electronic monitoring and algorithmic management are not regulated as working-condition issues; and protection for platform and remote workers remains incomplete. The article proposes an integrated reform model built around seven elements: express recognition of mental health and psychosocial risks; mandatory risk assessment and control; a qualified right to disconnect; transparency, consultation, and human review for digital monitoring and algorithmic decisions; confidential support and return-to-work measures; stronger social dialogue, inspection, and national data; and appropriately extended protection for platform workers. The proposed model treats mental health protection as a preventive labour-law obligation and a condition of sustainable digital transformation rather than as a discretionary employee benefit.

title: Green finance for sustainability: bibliometric analysis in global perspective
summary: Purpose Recent literature has focused on green finance in the form of investments and sustainability. This interest has arisen because of concerns over climate and emissions issues. Hence, this study aims to assess the current state of research on green finance and suggest future research directions. Design/methodology/approach Academic literature was sourced from the Scopus database (2000–2024). To ensure accuracy, specific inclusion and exclusion criteria were applied, yielding 1,865 articles. The selected articles were analysed using VOSviewer software and the Bibliometrix R package. Findings The study indicated that green finance research is no longer confined to the examination of environmental problems alone. Instead, it has progressed into an integrated framework linking policy interventions, technological innovation and financial instruments. Moreover, from a geographical perspective, green finance is moving from Western market-led models to Asian state-led sustainability models. Research limitations/implications This study used a combination of various analyses and presented future research areas for academics. A theoretical basis was also considered to verify the themes that emerged from the analysis. Practical implications Practitioners will have a clear understanding of green finance based on the themes identified in this study. The proposed themes and subthemes can be used as pointers in decision-making processes related to green finance. Mapping existing policies and regulations to the identified research themes reveals gaps. Insights from this type of mapping highlight the need for future government intervention in terms of policy and regulation. Originality/value Previous bibliometric studies have had a limited focus on combined analysis of authors, journals and countries, co-occurrence analysis of keywords, and clustering using co-citation analyses. In addition, the theoretical basis was not considered. These shortcomings were addressed in this study, and future research areas were identified and verified on a theoretical basis.

title: The Influence of Capital Market on Infrastructure Development in Nigeria
summary: The study investigated the influence of capital market on infrastructure development in Nigeria, which utilized a quasi-experimental research design and time series yearly data from 1981 to 2025. title: THE IMPACT OF TRANSFORMATIONAL LEADERSHIP AND GOOD CORPORATE GOVERNANCE ON JOB PERFORMANCE: A META-ANALYSIS
summary: Performance plays a significant role in achieving organizational goals, fostering competitiveness, and maintaining sustainability. Earlier investigations demonstrate that transformative leadership and sound corporate governance (GCG) considerably influence performance. Nevertheless, an exhaustive integration of empirical results is essential to clarify the intensity and coherence of this connection. This report use quantitative meta-analysis to assess the influence of transformative leadership and governance on performance outcomes. We rigorously identified 32 empirical research articles published between 2021 and 2026 from the Google Scholar, Scopus, and ScienceDirect databases. Utilizing JASP, we determined impact sizes and analyzed heterogeneity via a random-effects model. The assessment demonstrated that transformational leadership (r = 0.378) and GCG (r = 0.172) significantly positively impacted employee performance (p < 0.01). Transformational leadership exhibited a greater influence. The investigation identified diversity across the research and lacked evidence of publication bias. These conclusions are consistent with the prevailing research, underscoring the crucial impact of transformational leadership and GCG in elevating performance. The outcomes emphasize the importance of transformational leadership and effective corporate governance in boosting company performance. As a result, pragmatic advice involves establishing focused transformational leadership training and corporate policies that foster GCG to boost performance.

title: BRSR 2.0 and Mandatory ESG Assurance: Is India Moving towards Audit-based Sustainability Governance?
summary: In the span of just over a decade, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (“SEBI”) has moved India's listed firms from voluntary sustainability reporting towards a progressively mandatory, independently verified ESG ("Environmental, Social and Governance") disclosure regime. The launch in July 2023 of a new category of Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting (the “BRSR Core”), together with the ease-of-doing-business relaxations of March 2025, has introduced a hybrid ‘assessment or assurance’ paradigm that borrows both the vocabulary and, more significantly, the legal gravitas of statutory financial auditing. The scope of this paper is limited only to the Standard Core Disclosures for BRSR as required by SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 and does not include the voluntary ESG Ratings, ESG labelled investment products and environmental clearances granted for sectors under a dedicated approach. This paper analyses whether this shift amounts to a transformation toward audit-based sustainability governance in India. It argues that although SEBI has made ESG reporting a compliance requirement under the Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements Regulations, 2015, there has been no commensurate progress in Indian law regarding the allocation of responsibility for ESG statements and errors among directors, the audit committee, independent directors, assurance providers, and statutory auditors. Based on the analysis of India's corporate jurisprudence, SEBI's enforcement practices, and ESG-related assurance litigation in Australia and the United States, this paper argues that a dedicated statutory blueprint for ESG assurance in India is needed, and that assurance should be a separate regulatory function, with specific liability rules, to close the enforcement gap that currently leaves unverified sustainability claims unpunished.

title: How power advantage and digital intelligence reconfigure green supply chain efficiency: a dynamic QCA approach
summary: Purpose This study investigates how different dimensions of power advantage and digital intelligence combine to shape green supply chain (GSC) efficiency. Design/methodology/approach Using data from 140 Chinese listed manufacturing enterprises over the period 2015–2023, this study applies dynamic qualitative comparative analysis (QCA) to comprehensively examine the configurations associated with GSC efficiency. Findings Four configurations can lead to high GSC efficiency: market synergy management, organizational change leading, ecological network empowerment and professional authority allocation. The sufficiency of the four configurations exhibits limited temporal variation as policy and market conditions evolve. The first three configurations show greater empirical relevance among high-end equipment manufacturing enterprises, whereas the fourth configuration is more relevant among enterprises outside this industry and those located in non-key environmental protection cities. Additionally, configurations leading to low GSC efficiency result from mismatches and imbalances among antecedent conditions and are not symmetric with those leading to high GSC efficiency. Originality/value Drawing on power-dependence theory and complex systems theory, this study develops a configurational framework that treats market, technology and network power advantages, digital-intelligent equipment, digital-intelligent executives and fintech as antecedent conditions and GSC efficiency as the outcome. The findings contribute to deepening the understanding of power structures and provide a theoretical reference for constructing GSC systems in the digital intelligence era.

title: Digital Twins as Socio-Technical Decision Systems: A Comparative Systematic Review of Supply Chain Management and Healthcare
summary: Digital Twin (DT) technology is rapidly evolving from a digital representation of physical assets into a decision-support infrastructure that integrates real-time data, analytics, and simulation. However, existing research remains fragmented across application domains, limiting understanding of how DTs enable decision-making under different socio-technical conditions. This study presents a systematic literature review and decision-centric comparative analysis of DT applications in two contrasting decision environments: Supply Chain Management (SCM) and healthcare. Following a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) protocol, 193 peer-reviewed studies (95 SCM and 98 healthcare) were identified, screened, and synthesized across six analytical dimensions: application domains, technological integration, decision-making levels, business value, stakeholder involvement, and implementation challenges. The findings reveal fundamentally different decision logics despite a shared technological foundation based on Internet of Things (IoT), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and cloud computing. SCM-DTs primarily support coordination, optimization, resilience, and organizational scalability, whereas healthcare-DTs emphasize personalization, patient safety, and ethical governance under stringent regulatory constraints. Building on these findings, the study proposes a decision-centric comparative framework and a value–complexity perspective suggesting that value realization is increasingly associated with technological, organizational, and governance complexity as DT ecosystems mature. The paper advances the conceptualization of DTs as socio-technical decision systems and provides practical guidance for researchers, managers, and policymakers seeking responsible and effective digital transformation.

title: Short Term Debt Ratio and Environmental Disclosure: A Study of Oil and Gas Firms in Nigeria
summary: The study investigates the effect of short-term debt ratio on environmental disclosure of listed oil and gas firms in Nigeria. Descriptive statistics was utilized to describe the mean, median, standard deviation, kurtosis, skewness, maximum and minimum values and Panel Least Square (PLS) regression analysis was employed to test the hypothesis via E-Views 10 statistical software. The study upholds that short-term debt ratio has significant and positive effect on environmental disclosure of listed oil and gas firms in Nigeria. In line with the conclusion of this study, recommended that in order to sustain the positive relationship between short-term debt and environmental sustainability disclosure, this study suggests that firms should continue with the usage of short-term debt in financing operations so as to improve and sustain their financial performance.

title: Overconfident CEOs, Earnings Manipulation, and the Limits of Governance in Concentrated-Ownership Markets
summary: This study investigates the relationship between chief executive officer (CEO) overconfidence and earnings management in non-financial companies listed on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul) from 2018 to 2024. Using 686 firm-year observations from 98 firms in markets where measures of executive stock options are unavailable or inappropriate for researchers, we create a formative principal component composite (OC_COMPOSITE) comprising an excess investment residual, a relative compensation ratio, and a 3-year acquisition frequency index. The composite meets pre-specified validation criteria for pairwise correlations, variance inflation factors, eigenvalues, and factor loadings. CEO overconfidence is positively associated with absolute discretionary accruals and aggregate real earnings management in both firm- and year-fixed-effects regressions and System Generalised Method of Moments (GMM). Based on the preferred System GMM specifications, the estimated coefficients associated with a one-standard-deviation increase in OC_COMPOSITE are equivalent to approximately 38% of the sample mean of absolute discretionary accruals and 44% of the sample mean of aggregate real earnings management; these are mean-relative effect-size benchmarks, not literal percentage changes in the dependent variables. Big Four audit engagement attenuates the overconfidence–accrual association but does not significantly moderate the real-activities relationship, whereas ownership concentration strengthens the association across both earnings-management channels, particularly for real activities. The gender interaction is interpreted as suggestive because female-led firm-years are rare in the sample. A pre-/post-2021 comparison further indicates attenuation of the overconfidence–earnings management association in the later period, although the observational design and gradual temporal pattern preclude causal attribution to the 2021 reforms. The study extends behavioural corporate finance and upper echelons theory to a concentrated-ownership emerging-market setting and develops a transferable three-proxy approach to measuring CEO overconfidence in institutional environments where conventional option-based measures are unavailable.

title: ESG Strategies and CBAM Adaptation in Taiwan Industries: A Case Study on Building Sustainable Competitive Advantage
summary: This case study examines SW Company, a leading Taiwanese solar energy firm, to illustrate how Taiwanese businesses integrate Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles into their core operational strategies within the global push for sustainability, and to effectively address the challenges presented by the European Union Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM). SW Company's CBAM response strategy demonstrates a proactive approach, viewing the mechanism as an opportunity for innovation. This is evident in its efforts to optimize product design, enhance energy efficiency, diversify its product portfolio, and foster stronger international collaborations. Concurrently, SW Company actively pursues climate and sustainable finance strategies, including participation in carbon markets and green bond issuances, to reduce financing costs and enhance its sustainable brand image. The study concludes that SW Company's successful approach serves as a valuable model for other Taiwanese businesses, underscoring the critical need for supportive government policies to facilitate a more efficient and competitive sustainable transformation across the Taiwanese business sector. title: The Impact of Cyber Security on Nigerian Digital Economy
summary: The purpose of the research is to examine the impact of cybercrime on Nigeria Digital Economy. Literature study was used to collect data from various materials that include libraries, the internet, books, journals, magazine, and historical stories. Data were also collected from Federal Bureau of Information (FBI), United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), Economic and Financial Commission (EFCC) site, Nigeria Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) site, The Economist Intelligence Unit report, Federal Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy report, and World Bank report. Survey method that included questionnaire was used to find out the factors that were responsible for cybercrime in Nigeria. The analysis and discussion shows that digital economy will lead to new jobs, new forms of digital work, new opportunities in digital ecosystem, increased competition from local and foreign digital firms, enhanced productivity from data driven business models, greater control of value chains using platforms-based business models, more tax revenue resulting from increased economic activities. However, cybercrime poses a significant threat to Nigeria’s digital economy with far-reaching consequences for businesses, individuals and the nation as a whole. The rise of digital technologies has created new opportunities for cybercriminals to exploit vulnerabilities resulting in substantial financial losses, decline in investor confidence, damage to Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs), inhibited digital participation and damage to business reputation.

title: The integration of artificial intelligence and Industry 4.0 in digital supply chains: A systematic review of e-commerce evolution under Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030
summary: Background: Saudi Arabia prioritises adopting artificial intelligence (AI) and Industry 4.0 for e-commerce and digital supply chains under Vision 2030, but implementation and alignment with diversification goals remain insufficiently synthesised in the literature. Objectives: The study examines the impact of AI and automation on digital supply chains, identifies drivers and obstacles in Saudi Arabia’s e-commerce, and assesses their alignment with Vision 2030’s sustainability and diversification goals. Method: Following preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses, 30 peer-reviewed articles from 2020 to 2026 were reviewed from IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar, using bibliometric and thematic analysis. Results: Findings indicate that AI accounts for 46% of variability in sustainable performance; hybrid machine learning models reduce demand prediction error by 8.58% and achieve forecasting accuracy of up to 92%. Saudi Arabia’s 99% internet penetration supports Internet of Things development, but organisational barriers such as cultural resistance, cost, and job displacement (0.51) dominate adoption challenges over technical issues. Conclusion: Digitalisation success relies on technical and social systems, including government training and cybersecurity, to leverage AI for economic diversification beyond oil under Vision 2030. Contribution: The study connects national strategies to digital transformation, emphasising cybersecurity, workforce training, and the integration of technical and social systems, acknowledging immersive and decentralised tech as foundational for next-generation IoT and e-commerce.

title: Decision-Making in Power Supply Chains Considering Natural Hazards
summary: Natural hazards have a significant impact on the power supply chain and simultaneously affect the utilization efficiency of renewable energy. The joint effect of disaster probability and emergency procurement costs on pricing, renewable energy investment, and profit distribution within a two-echelon power supply chain remains underexplored. To fill this gap, we construct two game-theoretic models: Model S in a stable natural environment and Model D under natural hazards. The main conclusions are as follows: (1) In both scenarios, the profit level of the producer depends on the probability of natural hazards. When 0 < μ ≤ μ1, the producer earns a higher profit in Model S, whereas when μ1 < μ < 1, the producer earns a higher profit in Model D. The profit level of retailers depends on the unit procurement price of emergency supplies and the probability of natural hazards. (2) In a stable natural environment, the optimal wholesale price set by the power producer, the optimal retail price set by the electricity retailer, the demand for renewable energy electricity, the total electricity demand, and consumer surplus are all higher than in the scenario where a natural hazard occurs. In the scenario of a natural hazard, the profit of the players is determined by the proportion of renewable energy power supply and prevailing market demand conditions. (3) As the preference coefficient for renewable electricity increases, the retail price, electricity demand, profit of both players, and consumer surplus all rise. In contrast, the renewable energy investment cost coefficient has the opposite effect on them. Additionally, the demand for traditional energy power is positively correlated with the investment cost coefficient.

title: Predicting First Observed Appearance in a Corporate Governance Rating List and Subsequent Upgrades with Interpretable Machine Learning
summary: Corporate governance certification provides a public assessment of organizational practices. Previous research has primarily examined the relationship between certification and firm outcomes, while the timing of certification adoption represents a distinct prediction problem. This study examines whether the first observed appearance on a governance rating list and subsequent rating upgrades can be predicted using statutory accounting disclosures. Rating history is also incorporated into the upgrade model. The institutional setting is the Borsa Istanbul Corporate Governance Index, where licensed agencies evaluate four governance sections and eligibility is determined by published thresholds. The dataset combines rating records for 49 non-financial firms from 2013 to 2024 with financial statements from 438 listed non-financial firms. Two interpretable modeling modules employ an out-of-time design, with predictor variables measured before the corresponding outcomes. The entry module compares L2-regularized logistic regression, Firth-penalized logistic regression, and gradient-boosted trees within a discrete-time hazard specification. The trajectory module estimates next-year rating upgrade scores for rated firms using accounting information and rating history. Both linear entry models achieve areas under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve above 0.50, while the regularized logistic model shows a small positive difference in average precision relative to the training-prevalence benchmark. A single deflated firm-size measure provides discriminatory performance comparable to that of the multivariate entry models. The combined upgrade models achieve ROC areas close to 0.60, while models incorporating rating history achieve higher ROC areas than accounting-only models. Feature attributions also differ between the two tasks, with firm size playing a prominent role in entry predictions and rating history contributing more strongly to upgrade predictions. These findings identify the information sets associated with observed rating adoption and progression. The proposed framework provides rankings of candidate firms and feature-level explanations to support governance monitoring and outreach planning.

title: The Effect of Relational Resources on Supply Chain Robustness: The Moderating Role of Relational Capital
summary: Increasing supply chain disruptions have intensified the need for firms to develop capabilities that support operational continuity and effective responses to uncertainty. Although previous studies have examined supply chain robustness through operational and technological perspectives, limited attention has been given to how relational resources influence robustness and how relational capital shapes these relationships. This study examines the effects of resource complementarity and resource specificity on supply chain robustness and investigates the direct and moderating roles of relational capital among firms in the Greater Accra Region of Ghana. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted using structured questionnaires administered to supply chain managers. Of the 384 questionnaires distributed, 296 valid responses were used for analysis. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) was performed using SmartPLS. Resource complementarity positively influenced supply chain robustness (β = 0.714, p < 0.001), whereas resource specificity had a significant negative association with robustness (β = −0.305, p = 0.022). Relational capital had a positive direct effect on robustness (β = 0.618, p < 0.001). It also positively moderated the relationship between resource complementarity and robustness (β = 0.292, p < 0.001) and negatively moderated the relationship between resource specificity and robustness (β = −0.197, p = 0.012). The study concludes that relational resources contribute significantly to supply chain robustness, but their effects depend on the nature of the resources and the relational conditions surrounding their use. Firms should strengthen collaboration and combine complementary partner resources while managing relationship-specific investments carefully to avoid unnecessary constraints on operational flexibility.

title: The Moderating Effect of Audit Quality on the Relationship Between Internal Controls and Financial Reporting Quality of Non-Financial Companies Listed at The Nairobi Securities Exchange, Kenya
summary: This study examined whether audit quality moderates the relationship between internal control systems and financial reporting quality among non-financial companies listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE). Although internal controls are intended to support reliable reporting, their contribution may depend on the strength of external audit scrutiny. Using a positivist, quantitative explanatory longitudinal panel design, the study analysed secondary data from 26 non-financial firms over 2010–2025 (416 firm-year observations). Internal control systems were assessed through an Internal Control Disclosure Index (ICDI) based on the five COSO components. Audit quality was represented by a composite index incorporating auditor size, audit tenure and audit opinion; the use of audit opinion as an outcome-related indicator is a measurement limitation that should be considered when interpreting the index. Financial reporting quality was proxied by signed discretionary accruals estimated using the modified Jones model and reverse-coded so that values closer to zero indicated higher quality. The study used firm fixed-effects regressions with firm-clustered robust standard errors to estimate direct and interaction effects. The interaction between internal control systems and audit quality was positive and statistically significant (? = 1.038, p = .013), providing evidence that the association between internal controls and reporting quality varies with audit quality. The result supports rejection of the null hypothesis of no moderation, although it should be interpreted as an estimated conditional association rather than proof of causation. The study contributes Kenya-specific panel evidence on the complementary roles of internal controls and external audit in financial reporting governance.

title: ECONOMIC MECHANISMS FOR IMPROVING TAX ADMINISTRATION IN THE DIGITAL ECONOMY
summary: This article examines the theoretical and economic foundations of improving tax administration in the digital economy, as well as the organizational and economic aspects of introducing modern information and communication technologies into the activities of tax authorities. It explores the opportunities for simplifying interactions between taxpayers and government tax authorities, monitoring the fulfillment of tax obligations, forecasting tax revenues, and reducing the scale of the shadow economy through the digitalization of tax administration. The article also analyzes the impact of electronic invoices, online cash register systems, electronic tax services, and data analytics technologies on the efficiency of the tax system. Based on the research findings, economic and organizational recommendations are developed to advance digital tax administration.

title: Poultry meat safety and supply chain quality in Bani-Waleed restaurants
summary: Foodborne illnesses are caused mostly by the contaminated poultry products, which illnesses represent a critical public health challenge, particularly in the developing countries where the restaurant hygiene practices and regulatory authorities’ oversight over the hygiene are often inadequate. This study addresses the gap in microbiological safety data for the poultry dishes served at food service establishments in Bani-Waleed city located at the northwest of Libya where no prior peer reviewed bacteriological assessment was published before. Ten poultry meat samples (5 raw, 3 grilled, 2 boiled in broth) were collected from five fast-food restaurants (designated as the Restaurant 1, Restaurant 2, Restaurant 3, Restaurant 4, Restaurant 5) in Bani-Waleed city and transported to the Food Control Centre in Tripoli city under refrigeration (4 °C) within 5 hours. Quantitative microbiological analysis was performed using the decimal dilution plate technique on relevant selective media: MacConkey agar and Sorbitol MacConkey agar (SMAC) for Escherichia coli and E. coli O157: H7; Mannitol Salt Agar (MSA) for Staphylococcus aureus; and XLD agar for Salmonella spp. The systematic visual hygiene condition assessment of the five restaurants was conducted alongside a consumer survey administered to 177 restaurant customers. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS software. All raw meat samples (100 %) were contaminated with E. coli, with mean total bacterial counts of 9.68 × 103 ± 220 CFU/g. E. coli O157: H7 was detected in all raw meat samples and still persisted in three grilled samples obtained from the restaurants 2, 4, and 5 after cooking. Staphylococcus aureus was found in raw meat obtained from four restaurants (80 %) but this bacteria strain was eliminated after cooking. Salmonella was not found in all samples (0 %). Cooking significantly reduced total bacterial counts (p = 0.001), but the persistence of E. coli O157: H7 in the grilled chicken meat samples indicated inadequate cooking temperatures or post-cooking cross-contamination. Visual assessments revealed poor hygiene compliance, with all restaurants scoring below 65 %. A consumer survey indicated that 53 % of 177 participants experienced food poisoning symptoms after eating the restaurant meals. The results reveal serious microbiological safety hazards in poultry meat served in Bani- Waleed restaurants, induced by poor hygiene practices, inadequate cooking procedures, and insufficient regulatory authorities’ oversight. Urgent implementation of Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point (HACCP) principles, mandatory food handlers’ training, and development the strengthened health inception is recommended to ensure public health protection in the region.

title: Smart Multi-Species Milk Bank System (SM²BS) Integrating Cold Chain Management, Digital Traceability, and Nutritional Profiling of Cow, Goat, Sheep, Mare, and Buffalo Milk
summary: The Smart Multi-Species Milk Bank System (SM²BS) is proposed as an integrated digital platform to improve milk supply chain management through cold chain management, digital traceability, and nutritional profiling. This study adopts a qualitative approach involving literature review, observation of milk handling processes, and stakeholder discussions to identify operational challenges and develop a conceptual framework for managing cow, goat, sheep, mare, and buffalo milk. Building on the existing Smart Milk Bank System (SMBS) prototype and preliminary goat milk quality testing conducted with CV Cahaya Firdaus, the proposed system integrates batch identification, quality records, storage conditions, and comparative nutritional data. Its disruptive novelty lies in connecting multi-species nutritional intelligence with cold chain monitoring and end-to-end traceability within a unified digital ecosystem. The framework is expected to support improved transparency, quality management, inventory coordination, and informed decision-making across milk supply chains. However, the proposed multi-species functionality and its operational benefits require further implementation and validation. This study provides a conceptual foundation for developing a more integrated, data-driven milk bank system and strengthening dairy supply chain resilience.

title: Do AI and Lexicon-Based ESG Scores Converge? Evidence from IPO Prospectuses in an Emerging Market
summary: The growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) to evaluate Environmental, Social, Governance (ESG) scoring from corporate disclosures raises questions about alignment with conventional lexicon-based scores. Such alignment can be problematic as a lexicon-based approach quantifies the textual density using an ESG dictionary, while LLM-based scores are able to assess the thematic coverage of ESG themes. It remains unclear whether the two approaches produce comparable or distinct results when applied to the same corporate information. This paper examines the construct alignment between LLM-generated and lexicon-based ESG scores using 625 Indian IPO prospectuses issued between 2018 and 2024. A rebalanced dictionary of 630 terms measures disclosure intensity, while contextual scores are obtained by prompting a generative AI model. Both sets of scores are harmonised into quantile categories and compared using confusion matrices, correlation analysis, and chance-corrected agreement. The methods converge for the environmental dimension (EMR = 46.1%; weighted κ = 0.56) but diverge for social (28.2%) and governance (23.0%) disclosure, with only limited alignment overall (31.7%). The findings suggest the two approaches operationalise ESG differently, with implications for construct validity and transparency in ESG analytics.

title: Green Initiatives and Financial Performance: ESG Associations and Corporate Life-Cycle Contingencies in China’s Heavily Polluting Industries
summary: This study examines how green initiatives are associated with financial performance through a statistical indirect pathway involving environmental, social, and governance (ESG) assessment and whether that pathway varies across life-cycle stages. Using an unbalanced panel of 6579 firm-year observations from 1114 Chinese A-share firms in heavily polluting industries during 2015–2024, the analysis compares green investment, green innovation, green subsidy, and ISO 14001 certification within a common framework. Firm and year fixed-effects models with firm-clustered inference are combined with 5000 firm-cluster bootstrap replications and Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate adjustment. All four initiatives are positively associated with Huazheng ESG ratings. ESG ratings are positively associated with ROA and ROE, whereas a positive association with Tobin’s Q is not established. Each initiative exhibits a positive statistical indirect association with ROA through ESG, although total financial associations remain heterogeneous; green subsidy shows a negative contemporaneous total association with ROA. The mediated effects are economically modest: a one within-firm standard-deviation increase in each initiative corresponds to about 0.20–0.34% of a within-firm standard deviation of ROA through ESG. By contrast, a one within-firm standard-deviation increase in green subsidy is associated with a −0.133 percentage-point total ROA association. Corporate life cycle selectively conditions the pathway: ESG-mediated associations of green investment and green subsidy are significantly stronger in growth-stage firms than in mature or declining firms, while comparable stage differences are not established for green innovation or certification. The evidence distinguishes external sustainability assessment from immediate profitability and locates life-cycle dependence in resource-deployment-intensive green actions.

title: JAPAN’S POLICY ON FORMING INTERNATIONAL HYDROGEN SUPPLY CHAINS IN THE ASIA-PACIFIC REGION
summary: In the context of the global transition to a low-carbon development trajectory, hydrogen is becoming a key element of energy security and decarbonization of the economy. The article is devoted to the analysis of Japan’s policy on the formation of international hydrogen supply chains in the Asia-Pacific region. Japan’s limited domestic energy resources, heavy dependence on imports, and ambitious climate goals make cross-border hydrogen infrastructure a strategic priority for Tokyo. Japan considers the import of low-carbon hydrogen as a tool to ensure sustainable energy supply, diversify energy sources and strengthen technological leadership in promising industries.The paper shows that Japan currently plays a leading role in developing and implementing international hydrogen projects. It is actively building bilateral and multilateral agreements with Asia-Pacific countries, establishing specialized terminals, testing transport and storage technologies, and introducing national standards and certification systems. Increased attention is being paid to institutional mechanisms, public-private partnerships, and financial support that allow Japanese corporations to initiate and coordinate regional initiatives. The study demonstrates that Japan’s policy goes beyond purely energy objectives, forming a sustainable model of technological and economic cooperation capable of shaping the architecture of the future hydrogen trading market in the Asia-Pacific region.The potential remains within the framework of Russian-Japanese cooperation. Russia has significant resources for the production of low-carbon hydrogen, which, combined with Japanese technological and investment opportunities, creates objective conditions for launching joint pilot projects in the Russian Far East. Despite the difficult foreign policy environment, geographical proximity is a factor determining the long-term prospects for cooperation.

title: Convergent Digital, Quantum, Spectral Frameworks for Resilient Supply Chains and Sustainable Mobility
summary: This paper synthesizes a coherent research program spanning digital twins, artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain, quantum optimization, Industry 5.0, electric and solar-assisted vehicles, and a family of Fourier–Karhunen–Fourier (FKF) spectral transforms. Drawing on twenty-eight prior studies, the paper argues that resilience is no longer a purely organizational property; it is a coupled cyber-physical-spectral property that can be measured, optimized, and secured. Digital twins provide a living model of multi-echelon networks; AI and blockchain jointly raise transparency and green performance,; quantum annealing and related methods attack combinatorial bottlenecks in unit-load and disruption recovery problems,; and the FKF/FKL transform family supplies a shift-invariant spectral calculus for lead-time, inventory, and resonance phenomena –. Mobility work on battery sizing, materials, solar hybrids, and intelligent transport, closes the loop between energy, vehicles, and freight. The contribution is an integrated agenda: sense with IoT, twin the network, optimize with AI and quantum, certify with blockchain, and diagnose dynamics with FKF spectra.

title: Environmental, Social and Governance Disclosures and the Value of Listed Nigerian Firms
summary: This study examined the effect of environmental, social and governance (ESG) disclosures on the value of listed Nigerian firms. Specifically, it investigated the effects of environmental disclosure index (EDI), social responsibility expenditure ratio (SRER), board independence ratio (BIR), and audit independence ratio (AIR) on firm value measured by Tobin’s Q. The study adopted an ex post facto research design with a quantitative panel-data approach. The population comprised firms listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group, while purposive sampling was used to select ten firms from the manufacturing and oil and gas sectors. The sampled firms were Dangote Cement Plc, BUA Cement Plc, Nestlé Nigeria Plc, Nigerian Breweries Plc, Lafarge Africa Plc, Seplat Energy Plc, TotalEnergies Marketing Nigeria Plc, Oando Plc, Conoil Plc, and MRS Oil Nigeria Plc. Secondary data were obtained from published annual reports and financial statements covering 2016–2025, producing 100 balanced firm-year observations. Data were analysed using panel least squares regression in EViews 13.0. Descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, residual cross-sectional dependence, ADF panel unit-root and Pedroni panel cointegration tests were conducted. The Redundant Fixed Effects and Correlated Hausman tests guided model selection. The results showed that EDI had a positive but insignificant effect on Tobin’s Q (coefficient = 1.3590; p = 0.2270). SRER had a positive and significant effect (coefficient = 0.0976; p = 0.0052), while BIR also had a positive and significant effect (coefficient = 0.1751; p = 0.0119). AIR exerted a positive and significant effect on Tobin’s Q (coefficient = 0.2325; p = 0.0061). The fixed-effects model was statistically significant (F = 932.6305; p = 0.0000) and explained 89.30% of the variation in firm value (R² = 0.892957). The study concluded that social responsibility expenditure, board independence and audit independence significantly enhanced firm value, whereas environmental disclosure alone did not produce a statistically significant valuation effect. The study recommended improved environmental disclosure quality, strategic social responsibility expenditure, stronger board independence and enhanced audit independence among listed Nigerian firms.

title: Digital Transformation and Operational Efficiency in Petroleum Enterprises: Mechanisms and Panel Evidence from Chinese A-Share-Listed Firms, 2008–2024
summary: Amid the rapid development of the digital economy and China’s carbon-peaking and carbon-neutrality goals, digital transformation has emerged as a critical pathway for petroleum enterprises to improve quality and efficiency. However, the mechanisms linking digital transformation to operational efficiency in the petroleum industry remain insufficiently understood. Using an unbalanced panel of 45 Chinese A-share-listed petroleum firms over the 2008–2024 period, this study examines the direct effect of digital transformation on operational efficiency, the mediating roles of factor-utilization efficiency and technological innovation capability, and the moderating effects of ownership and firm size. The results show that digital transformation is significantly and positively associated with operational efficiency. Among its dimensions, digital applications exert the strongest enabling effect, whereas the digital-achievements dimension may suppress operational efficiency in the short run. The relationship also operates through two mediation channels: technological innovation capability transmits the effect significantly for both efficiency measures, whereas factor-utilization efficiency transmits it significantly for total asset turnover only. By contrast, the moderating effects of ownership and firm size are not statistically significant in the current estimates: the interaction terms of digital transformation with state ownership and with firm size are insignificant for both efficiency measures. These findings clarify how digital transformation affects operational efficiency in petroleum enterprises and provide evidence for designing more effective digital transformation strategies in the energy sector.

title: Supply chain antifragility capabilities: a systematic literature network analysis and conceptual framework
summary: Purpose Supply chains are essential to economic growth in many industries. However, their complexity and slow response to market changes leave them vulnerable to environmental disruptions. The concept of antifragility explains how organizations can withstand and even thrive during disruptions. The goal of this paper is to review and consolidate the literature on supply chain antifragility and derive a conceptual framework that illustrates how antifragility-oriented capabilities can transform disruptions into long-lasting performance improvements. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature network analysis (SLNA) and a keyword analysis were conducted on articles related to antifragility and supply chain capabilities published in the Scopus database between 2012 and June 2025. Based on the resulting thematic clusters identified through SLNA and keyword analysis, additional literature, and dynamic capability theory, a novel conceptual framework for supply chain antifragility was developed. Findings The SLNA reveals three principal thematic clusters: supply chain vulnerabilities, supply chain enablers, and supply chain capabilities for antifragility. These thematic clusters converge in an integrative conceptual framework showing how antifragility emerges from interactions among disruption drivers and triggers, technological and informational enablers, and antifragility capabilities. These factors collectively facilitate enhanced supply chain antifragility outcomes. Originality/value Introduced in 2012, antifragility offers an alternative perspective to the traditional concepts of robustness and resilience. It has only recently been applied to supply chains, which are subject to common disorder and disruption. By examining the concept in this context and reviewing relevant work, the analyses and conceptual framework developed in this study provide a comprehensive overview, establish a critical foundation for future research, and inform how to take advantage of supply chain antifragility.
