title: Climate stressors, green finance and food productivity: comparative evidence from Asia and Africa
summary: Purpose Climate stressors pose a significant challenge to global food systems by influencing food productivity. This study examines the impact of climate-related factors, specifically carbon footprint and temperature, on food productivity, while also exploring the moderating role of green finance in major economies across Asia and Africa from 1990 to 2022. Design/methodology/approach The study employed yearly World Bank data using the panel Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) Model. This technique examines variables integrated at distinct levels (order 0 and order 1) and captures within-country variability while addressing cross-country variances and country-specific shocks. Findings The empirical results reveal divergent regional pathways. In Asia, carbon footprint exhibits a marginally significant negative impact on food productivity, whereas temperature surprisingly demonstrates a significant positive effect. Conversely, in Africa, carbon footprint exerts a strongly significant negative influence. Crucially, green finance emerges as a statistically significant and positive driver of food productivity in both regions, highlighting its potential as a key tool for building climate-resilient agri-food systems. Practical implications The findings emphasize the need for region-specific climate adaptation and mitigation strategies, particularly in African economies where agricultural systems remain highly climate-sensitive. Policymakers should strengthen green financial frameworks and invest in technological innovation to promote climate-resilient agriculture, enhance food security and achieve long-term sustainability goals. Originality/value This study provides the first known comparative, cross-regional analysis of the linkages between carbon footprint, green finance and food productivity in Asia and Africa. Employing a panel ARDL approach over 33 years, it offers novel insights into the temporal dynamics and regional disparities that inform targeted investment and policy decisions in the global agri-food sector.

title: Predicting ESG adoption among Malaysian SMEs using explainable machine learning
summary: Abstract Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) considerations are increasingly embedded in regulatory frameworks, financial markets, and corporate strategy worldwide. While large listed firms have been the primary focus of ESG reporting requirements, small and medium enterprises (SMEs) play a central role in employment, supply chains, and regional development, particularly in emerging economies. In Malaysia, SMEs account for the vast majority of business establishments, yet ESG adoption remains uneven across firms. This study examines which non-practice firm-level characteristics are associated with ESG adoption classification among formal-sector Malaysian SMEs using explainable machine learning. The sample of 457 firms is drawn from a bank-linked stakeholder network, so it over-represents formal-sector, bank-connected SMEs, and the outcome is self-declared. The survey records ESG adoption on a four-level scale (fully, partially, planning to, or not implementing), which is recoded into a binary adopter/non-adopter target for the main analysis; it reflects reported adoption status rather than a verified measure of ESG performance. Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and Explainable Boosting Machine (EBM) are compared using nested cross-validation with all preprocessing fitted inside the cross-validation pipeline. On the held-out test set of 92 observations, Random Forest recorded the highest discrimination point estimates (ROC-AUC = 0.853; adopter-positive PR-AUC = 0.904). Paired bootstrap comparisons showed higher Random Forest discrimination than XGBoost and EBM, but did not distinguish Random Forest from Logistic Regression on ROC-AUC. No model was uniformly superior across all reported metrics, and the estimates remain imprecise because of the small held-out sample. On a common measure of variable-level importance computed for all four models, several predictors recur near the top, most consistently the use of financial consultants as an ESG advisory source, ownership type, and company type or market orientation, followed by programme-awareness and funding-intent variables. When the models are refitted across cross-validation folds, the rankings shift and few variables hold a fixed position, so these are reported as recurring but unstable predictive signals rather than a stable set of determinants. The results are predictive and non-causal: the model identifies firm characteristics associated with higher predicted adoption probability, not causal mechanisms. Performance is evaluated internally, with no external validation, so the model is exploratory and not ready for operational allocation or policy deployment. Within that scope, the findings offer an interpretable basis for exploratory segmentation of formal-sector, bank-connected SMEs and may help generate hypotheses for more targeted sustainability support.

title: Automated Validation of Service-Oriented and API-Based Enterprise Systems for Reliable Digital Transformation in Saudi Arabia
summary: The extent to which Saudi Arabia is undergoing a digital transformation now relies on enterprise platforms that are put together using APIs, service-oriented components, microservices, identity services, data stores, and capabilities that are managed externally. This architectural modularity speeds up the delivery process but at the same time spreads out any potential failures across the interface contracts, the parameter dependencies, the workflow state, the data semantics, the performance, the security, and the runtime operations. A service may therefore pass local tests yet the entire public or enterprise transaction end-to-end will still be unreliable. This review brings together recent evidence on automated validation methods that have been published between 2020 and 2025 and presents an integrated assurance framework aimed at achieving reliable digital transformation in Saudi Arabia. The review looks at specification-driven API testing, dependency-aware test generation, contract testing, cross-service functional and robustness testing, performance verification, security testing, and observability. Thirty peer-reviewed sources, verified by DOI, were chosen as part of a protocol-led evidence review with a focus on automation, architectural relevance, empirical support, and suitability for use in enterprise systems. The synthesis indicates that no one test technique offers enough assurance for distributed digital services; reliability instead comes from a layered body of evidence that links interface correctness with stateful workflows, service interoperability, resilience in the face of failure, security controls, and production telemetry. The paper suggests a seven-stage automated validation architecture and a continuous-assurance maturity pathway which transform diverse evidence into clear decisions regarding releases and governance. For Saudi organisations, the framework stresses interoperability, service continuity, auditable changes, and evidence-based risk control, thus connecting software engineering practice with the level of operational reliability required by national digital transformation programmes.

title: Issues Regarding the Protection of Digital Assets in International Investment Law —Focusing on the Determination of the Investment Eligibility of Digital Assets
summary: The deepening development of the digital economy has made data assets a core vehicle of value for cross-border investment; however, traditional international investment law, which originated in the era of tangible assets, faces significant institutional tensions when determining whether digital assets constitute protected investments. Centered on the determination of the investment eligibility of digital assets, this paper focuses on three core legal challenges: the interpretation of investment definition clauses, the application of the Salini objective standard, and the determination of the territorial requirement. Through a systematic review of existing literature and an analysis of recent arbitration cases, such as Nexo v. Bulgaria and Einarsson v. Canada, this study reveals the normative conflict between the traditional treaty framework and the digital reality. This study finds that a balance should be sought between legal certainty and dynamic adaptability. It advocates for a typological approach to distinguishing between operational data assets and purely speculative crypto-assets, while retaining the basic function of the territorial requirement but interpreting it flexibly, replacing the requirement for physical establishment with a substantive economic connection. From a Chinese perspective, incremental experimentation with bilateral and regional rules represents a pragmatic path to participating in the digital transformation of international investment law.

title: Does ESG protect profitability in a crisis? Evidence from US industrial firms during COVID-19
summary: Using the COVID-19 pandemic as a common macroeconomic shock to which firms were differentially exposed, we investigate whether pre-crisis environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance was associated with corporate financial resilience, measured through return on assets (ROA). Two competing directional hypotheses are evaluated: the insurance-value hypothesis (H1a), under which accumulated stakeholder trust protects profitability in crises, and the short-run cost hypothesis (H1b), under which relatively rigid ESG-related commitments depress accounting returns when demand contracts. Using a panel of 70 US industrial firms over 2012–2021 (690 firm-year observations), a two-way fixed-effects (TWFE) difference-in-differences (DiD) framework compares changes in ROA across firms with stronger versus weaker pre-crisis ESG performance. The results are consistent with the short-run cost hypothesis: a one-standard-deviation higher pre-crisis ESG score is associated with an approximately 1.06 percentage-point larger relative decline in crisis-period ROA (continuous specification, p = 0.006), and high-ESG firms experienced a 1.97 percentage-point relative decline compared to low-ESG counterparts (p = 0.019; 95% confidence interval (CI) = −3.60 to −0.33; N = 70 firms), approximately 24% of mean ROA. Dynamic event-study estimates show no differential pre-trends and significant high-ESG differentials in both 2020 and 2021; the penalty is unchanged by controls for research-and-development (R&D) and advertising intensity, is imprecisely larger in the most pandemic-exposed industries in a triple-difference specification, and is attenuated within industry-by-year cells. Pillar-level estimates are precision-limited nulls. Where included, financial leverage is the strongest single predictor of crisis-period profitability. The findings are interpreted through a sustainability trade-off mechanism in which environmental and social commitments behave like fixed capacity investments that build relational value over the long run but increase operating leverage in the short run; they identify a robust profitability pattern consistent with this mechanism, rather than a direct evaluation of it, and caution against treating ESG ratings as guarantees of short-run accounting resilience.

title: State capacity, blame avoidance and environmental justice in China’s recentralized environmental governance
summary: Conventional wisdom suggests that strong state capacity improves policy implementation and environmental justice while reducing blame politics. Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork in China, we argue that state capacity can instead redistribute blame and environmental injustice. We conceptualize environmental state capacity and its variation and unevenness by integrating policy outputs and outcomes with three dimensions: administrative, extractive, and coercive. While the clean energy transition project in Hebei exhibited strong capacity across three dimensions, Shanxi’s safe water supply project displayed strong administrative capacity, alongside weak extractive and coercive capacity. We find that different configurations of state capacity shape local officials’ implementation and blame-avoidance strategies by altering their assessment of political risk under authoritarian accountability. Both campaign-style implementation and ‘minimum compliance’ prioritized managing political risk over substantive environmental outcomes and justice, displacing costs onto marginalized rural communities. These displaced costs were followed by public backlash and a new, reactive round of blame politics.

summary: The article examines the current state, key challenges and prospects of the digital transformation of the Ukrainian economy in the unique conditions of martial law and European integration processes. The relevance of the topic is due to the fact that digital transformation is not only a factor in increasing the competitiveness of the national economy, but also a tool for ensuring its stability in conditions of military aggression, as well as an integral part of the process of Ukraine's integration into the European Union. In the theoretical aspect, scientific approaches to defining the digital economy are systematized, its key drivers and properties are identified, in particular, endogenous data generation and non-competitiveness of their use, which fundamentally distinguish the digital economy from the traditional one. It is substantiated that in modern scientific discourse there is no established definition of the digital economy, which complicates its quantitative assessment and comparative analysis. Four groups of challenges have been identified that hinder digital transformation: infrastructure and security (physical destruction of infrastructure, escalation of cyber threats, risks of digital sovereignty); social and human resources (digital skills deficit, IT brain drain, structural unemployment); institutional and regulatory (incomplete harmonization with the EU, policy fragmentation, lack of systematized data); organizational and financial (low digitalization of SMEs, limited financial resources, low investment activity in scientific research). Overcoming these challenges requires systemic coordination of all levels of government, the use of international technical assistance tools and constant monitoring of progress based on DESI indicators. The scientific novelty of the results obtained lies in the comprehensive analysis of the digital transformation of the Ukrainian economy under martial law using a detailed SWOT analysis and the construction of three development scenarios with quantitative forecast indicators, as well as the justification of strategic priorities for the forced scenario of the “digital leap”. The practical significance of the study is that the proposed approaches and recommendations can be used by state authorities to form an effective digital development policy under martial law and post-war recovery, by business – to determine digital adaptation strategies, and by the scientific community - as a basis for further research in the field of the digital economy.

title: EU–Central Asia Critical Raw Materials: From Partnership to Supply-Chain Security
summary: Executive Summary Critical raw materials (CRMs) have advanced in just a few years from a specialized industrial niche topic to the centre of geopolitical discussions. China's tightened export controls, culminating in its extraterritorial measures announced in October 2025, have made supply security an urgent strategic priority for the European Union. Against this backdrop, Central Asia has emerged as a key partner in the EU's efforts, to diversify its supply chains and reduce critical dependencies. This growing partnership is anchored in the EU's strategic partnerships with Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan and has been reinforced by the 2025 EU–Central Asia Summit in Samarkand and President Tokayev's visit to Brussels in June 2026. Building on Global Gateway and the Team Europe approach, the EU has developed a more comprehensive policy and financing framework for securing critical raw materials, notably through the Critical Raw Materials Act and the subsequent RESourceEU Action Plan, alongside the launch of its first Strategic Projects. With the framework now largely in place, the task ahead is delivery.

title: A Study on the Relationship Between the Digital Economy, Industrial Relocation, and Labor Migration
summary: Digitalized economy has been revamping the world industrial division of labor together with driving industrial relocation by geographical relocation of industries into digital restructuring of industries chains. Being one of the main factors influencing the process of industrial relocation, labor migration will undergo significant change in the patterns and determinants of migration. It is evident that digital tech alters the spatial logic of labor migration by reducing the cost of information and transactions as well as industrial relocations keep moving the regional labor force overtime due to the creation of job opportunities and the shifting nature of skill demands. The research suggests that the results of this study would help to enhance the digital infrastructure in the interior areas and improve the policies on talents in order to bring in skilled employees. Meanwhile, firms should embrace remote-work models to reduce unnecessary geographic moves. Crucially, targeted digital training is needed for low-skilled migrants, so they are not left behind. The present analysis offers empirical support to the concept that there are new features and processes of migration in a digital economy environment, offering a reference for formulating regional coordinated development strategies and labor market policies.

title: АНТИКРИЗОВЕ СТРАТЕГІЧНЕ ПЛАНУВАННЯ ДІЯЛЬНОСТІ ПІДПРИЄМСТВ
summary: In the current conditions of economic instability, global transformations, wartime challenges, and growing uncertainty, ensuring the sustainable functioning of enterprises is becoming increasingly important. The dynamism of the external environment, technological changes, market instability, shifts in demand, and disruptions to supply chains necessitate the improvement of logistics process management. Under such conditions, logistics management serves as an integrated mechanism for coordinating and optimizing material, financial, informational, and other flows. The article examines the theoretical foundations of logistics management and its role in ensuring enterprise efficiency and adaptability. Its consideration as an integrated system for managing flow processes aimed at ensuring their coordination, continuity, and rational use of resources is substantiated. Particular attention is paid to the digitalization of logistics, modern monitoring and analytical tools, and information support for managerial decision-making. The integration of ESG principles into the logistics management system is examined based on an analysis of the non-financial reporting of DHL Group, Maersk, DB Schenker, Kuehne+Nagel, and FedEx. Using content analysis, cross-case analysis, SWOT analysis, and conceptual modeling, 67 ESG initiatives were systematized according to environmental, social, and governance components. The study substantiates the feasibility of transitioning to an integrated logistics management model that combines economic efficiency, digitalization, resilience, and ESG orientation, contributing to enterprise adaptability, optimization of flow processes, and long-term sustainability. These approaches are aimed at strengthening the alignment of logistics decisions with the overall enterprise management system and improving resource utilization. Their practical application contributes to the formation of a flexible logistics system capable of effective functioning in a changing and risk-prone environment. A systemic approach to combining digital tools and ESG practices expands the enterprise’s capacity to manage risks and respond promptly to changes in the logistics environment. This creates conditions for improving the quality of managerial decisions, strengthening competitive positions, and ensuring sustainable enterprise development in the long term.

title: FROM DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION TO ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: A NEW PARADIGM OF GLOBAL JOURNALISM
summary: The contemporary media industry is undergoing one of the most profound transformations in the history of mass communication. Digital platforms, social networks, mobile technologies, big data, algorithmic distribution systems and, most recently, generative artificial intelligence have fundamentally changed the production, distribution and consumption of information. The traditional model in which professional media institutions controlled the principal channels of information has evolved into a complex digital ecosystem where journalists, media organisations, technology platforms, bloggers, influencers, artificial intelligence systems and ordinary users simultaneously participate in the creation and circulation of content. This article examines the transformation of mass media in the context of digitalisation, technological innovation and the rapid development of artificial intelligence. Particular attention is paid to the integration of generative AI into newsroom processes, including information gathering, transcription, translation, data analysis, content production, fact-checking, personalisation and audience engagement. The study argues that artificial intelligence should not be interpreted merely as an instrument of automation. Rather, it represents a structural factor capable of changing journalistic workflows, professional competencies, editorial responsibility, media economics and the relationship between media institutions and their audiences. At the same time, AI-driven journalism generates significant professional and ethical risks, including algorithmic bias, hallucinated information, deepfakes, synthetic content, copyright disputes and the possible erosion of public trust. The article concludes that the future competitiveness and social legitimacy of media organisations will depend not simply on technological adoption, but on their ability to combine innovation with professional standards, human editorial oversight, transparency and accountability.

title: Digital transformation and workforce resilience in social enterprises: governance for crisis readiness
summary: Purpose This study examines how digital transformation, workforce resilience and governance integration influence crisis readiness in social enterprises. It explores capability-building as a potential mechanism connecting digital transformation and governance with crisis readiness, while governance maturity and ecosystem collaboration are considered contextual conditions that may shape these relationships. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative design combined a comprehensive literature review of forty peer-reviewed studies with six semi-structured interviews involving governance, workforce and digital transformation leaders. Inductive coding identified three themes: governance for crisis readiness, digital transformation enablers and workforce resilience routines, interpreted through institutional theory and dynamic capability theory. Findings Governance embedded in digital workflows strengthens reliability and accountability. Capability-building routines such as micro-drills, peer learning, and digital literacy translate strategy into continuity outcomes. Ecosystem partnerships and institutional maturity amplify these effects by improving interoperability, resource sharing and collective learning. Practical implications Integrating governance controls within digital systems and aligning workforce development with feedback and monitoring enhances readiness, transparency and long-term sustainability. Originality/value This study develops a mechanism-informed conceptual framework that integrates governance maturity, digital transformation and workforce capability to explain potential pathways toward crisis readiness in social enterprises. It identifies capability-building as a proposed explanatory mechanism and ecosystem conditions as contextual influences, offering an integrative foundation for future empirical testing.

title: Green HRM and Green Servant Leadership: Enhancing Employee Performance through Green Innovation
summary: Purpose— This study examines the influence of Green Human Resource Management (Green HRM) on employee performance, with Green Innovation as a mediator and Green Servant Leadership (GSL) as a moderator, in Bangladesh’s ready-made garment (RMG) sector. Method— A quantitative approach was employed using data collected from 180 RMG employees through a structured questionnaire. SPSS 27 and AMOS 24 were used for descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA). Findings— The findings indicate that Green HRM positively influences employee performance, with Green Innovation acting as a mediator. GSL moderates the relationship between Green HRM and employee performance, strengthening the positive influence of Green HRM on performance. Conclusion and Implications— The study highlights the importance of integrating Green HRM, Green Innovation, and GSL to enhance employee performance in the RMG sector. RMG companies should incorporate sustainable practices into their HRM and leadership approaches to support innovation and performance. Future research could examine other sectors to assess the generalizability of the findings. Originality/Value— This study contributes context-specific evidence from Bangladesh’s RMG sector by integrating Green Innovation as a mediator and GSL as a moderator in the relationship between Green HRM and employee performance. It offers practical insights into aligning HRM and leadership practices with sustainability objectives in an emerging economy.

title: Social Marketing Strategies in the Pharmaceutical Industry, Characteristics and Impact; a scoping review
summary: Objective: To describe the social marketing strategies implemented by the pharmaceutical industry and their potential impact on consumer behavior and access to medicines, through a scoping review.Methods: A scoping review was conducted following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines.For data collection, scientific articles published between 2006 and 2025 in English and Spanish were selected using the PCC criteria (Population, Concept, Context), which are recommended for this type of research.The databases consulted were SciELO, Google Scholar, and PubMed.Articles published in peer-reviewed academic journals were included if their title, abstract, or keywords contained at least one of the descriptors used in the search equation.Results: Four categories of analysis emerged: 1) marketing and positioning, 2) corporate social responsibility, communication, and ethics, 3) digital transformation and innovation, and 4) pharmacy and access to medicines.A critical inflection point was identified, highlighting the intersection of access to medicines with the role of community pharmacies, which are implementing strategies to balance social commitments with commercial objectives. Conclusions:The pharmaceutical industry's social marketing strategies can be multidimensional.They have evolved from traditional corporate positioning to emerging categories that integrate ethics, digital transformation, and public health innovation.The current challenge lies in balancing business viability with the population's health and social needs.

title: Review of Transfer Learning Techniques for Cybersecurity in Digital Supply Chain Systems: Models, Applications, and Challenges
summary: The increasing complexity of digital supply chain systems introduces dynamic cybersecurity challenges that traditional machine learning approaches often fail to address due to their reliance on domain-specific labeled data. Transfer Learning (TL) has emerged as a promising paradigm to overcome these limitations by enabling knowledge reuse across domains, thereby enhancing cyber threat detection and adaptability. Guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) framework, this review systematically examines TL-based approaches applied to cybersecurity within digital supply chain environments. The study identifies key TL paradigms domain adaptation, inductive learning, transductive learning, and deep transfer learning and analyzes their roles in securing critical components of the digital ecosystem. The findings categorize research efforts into four major focus areas: network security, information security, web application security, and Internet of Things (IoT) security. Furthermore, the review highlights a significant surge in publications from 2020 onward, reflecting the growing scholarly and practical interest in TL-driven cybersecurity solutions. It concludes by identifying existing research gaps and proposing future directions for developing adaptive and intelligent cross-domain cybersecurity frameworks aimed at strengthening the resilience of digital supply chain systems.

title: Disclosed Green Supply Chain Practices and Recorded ISO 14001 Transitions in Chinese Listed Companies
summary: Disclosed green supply chain practices and environmental certification may share organizational antecedents without implying improved environmental outcomes. Using licensed CSMAR records for Chinese listed companies, we distinguish recorded certification transitions from persistent status and compare industry-and-year with firm-and-year fixed effects. The main risk set contains 18,424 firm-years recorded as not certified in the preceding calendar year, including 2121 subsequent affirmative records. Each additional prior-year disclosed practice is associated with a 1.423-percentage-point higher transition probability with industry-and-year effects and a 0.827-percentage-point difference with firm-and-year effects (95% confidence interval: 0.133–1.522 percentage points). A stricter no-earlier-observed-certification sensitivity is less precise and its firm-effect interval includes zero. Firm-disjoint comparisons assess stability within previously explored data, not independent external replication. Negative inventory and fixed-asset turnover associations weaken under alternative scales, and validation-sample firm-effect operational estimates are imprecise. A post-review extension to four disclosed emission quantities yields no association surviving the multiplicity correction specified for that extension; selective coverage and inconsistent reporting boundaries further limit inference. These findings provide an observational benchmark for formal governance rather than evidence of first-ever certification, causal effects or substantive environmental improvement.

title: The Impact of Investor Sentiment on Earnings Management and Financial Disclosure Behavior: Evidence from China’s A-Share Market
summary: Purpose: To evaluate whether investor sentiment influences voluntary disclosure and earnings-management decisions of Chinese A-share firms. Methods: Using industry-adjusted Tobin's Q as a firm-level valuation pressure or sentiment proxy, based on 14,081 firm-years of data from Chinese A-share-listed companies between 2013 and 2023. The measurement of earnings management is centered on performance-related fit indicators. Results: When sentiment is high, profitable firms tend to report more positive earnings and issue disclosures more frequently, compared to loss-making firms. Conclusion: Overall, evidence indicates that the Chinese A-share market tends to exhibit behavioral fluctuations in response to investors' emotional sentiments.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Emergency Medical Supply Request Regulation in Healthcare Supply Chains
summary: Public health emergencies place acute pressure on medical supply systems. This study develops Med-iDR-MARL, a hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework for regulating hospital requests before allocation. Regional incentives influence hospital responses for deferrable (DD) and reducible (RD) demand, while a local scheduler retains non-deferrable (ND) demand and applies hospital-level service bounds. Across 20 simulated 30-day windows, the framework reduced DD/RD requests by 37.71% with mean incentive expenditure of CNY 274,844.23, compared with 31.03% and CNY 350,038.43 for Rule-Adaptive. Independent hospital-agent deep Q-network learning achieved greater reduction, lower expenditure, and better pooled reduction per unit expenditure. The proposed framework also had the highest peak-to-average ratio despite lower absolute peaks than No-DR. In a separate five-seed ablation, removing the minimum-service guard increased the hospital-day violation rate from zero to 58.95%. Local scheduler diagnostics found feasible solutions in 132,000 tested states but material optimality gaps and no consistent runtime advantage over vectorized exact enumeration. The results identify conditional efficiency and service trade-offs. The Shanghai COVID-19 series supplies an external risk trajectory; hospital behavior, clinical outcomes, and operational logistics remain unvalidated.

title: Decarbonizing the Food Supply Chain in Emerging Market Economies: A Transition Management Framework for Carbon Neutrality
summary: ABSTRACT Decarbonizing the food supply chain in emerging market economies is vital for meeting national and global carbon neutrality commitments. This study identifies 15 key challenges hindering this transition and examines their structural interrelationships using interpretive structural modeling. The results identify lack of robust government policies and regulations, lack of low‐carbon facilities, and lack of R&D capabilities as the most influential challenges hindering the decarbonization transition. Grounded in transition management theory, these challenges are hierarchically organized into three interconnected transition levels: formulating carbon neutrality programs, deploying carbon neutrality measures, and implementing carbon neutrality practices. Further, based on the best‐worst method and VIKOR analyses, strategies including policy and regulatory framework, supply chain optimization and digitalization, and research and innovation ecosystem emerge as the highest‐priority strategic interventions. Thus, this study provides a theoretically grounded and practically actionable roadmap for businesses, policymakers, and other stakeholders seeking to accelerate the transition toward a carbon‐neutral food supply chain.

title: The impact of top management team regulatory focus on accounting conservatism
summary: Purpose Drawing on regulatory focus theory, this study aims to examine how top management teams' (TMTs) motivational orientations (promotion versus prevention focus) influence accounting conservatism and further explores the internal and external situational conditions that shape this relationship. Design/methodology/approach Using textual analysis to quantify TMT regulatory focus from management discussion and analysis (MD&A) across Chinese A-listed firms, this study applies multivariate regression analysis to assess the impact of regulatory focus on accounting conservatism. Findings Our results show that promotion-focused TMTs are more likely to diminish accounting conservatism, whereas prevention-focused TMTs enhance it. TMT restricted stock (internal situational factor) attenuates both the negative effect of promotion focus and the positive effect of prevention focus on accounting conservatism. Analyst coverage (external situational factor) weakens the negative effect of promotion focus on conservatism while amplifying the positive effect of prevention focus. Further subgroup analyses reveal that the effects of TMT regulatory focus are more pronounced in non-SOEs and firms with lower ownership concentration and are significantly moderated by auditor industry expertise and product-market competition, highlighting the role of internal governance and external market factors as important boundary conditions. Originality/value This study introduces TMT regulatory focus as a novel psychological determinant of accounting conservatism, shifting the literature beyond observable demographic proxies to the motivational drivers of managerial reporting behavior. Furthermore, it identifies two actionable governance levers that interact with TMT motivational orientations, offering a more nuanced framework for corporate governance and compensation design.

title: A hybrid data-driven and qualitative approach for critical factor identification in pharmaceutical supplier selection: safeguarding the continuity of pharmaceutical in disruption-prone settings
summary: Purpose This study aims to develop a comprehensive and integrated approach for identifying and prioritizing critical factors influencing pharmaceutical supplier selection and supply chain performance, with direct implications for health system resilience and access to essential medicines. By positioning supplier selection as an upstream determinant of preparedness, the study addresses the concerns of humanitarian and health supply chain actors that depend on commercial pharmaceutical suppliers for the uninterrupted availability of essential medicines during disruptions and emergencies. Design/methodology/approach A hybrid methodology is adopted, combining Principal Component Analysis (PCA), a machine learning-based dimensionality reduction technique and qualitative analysis using NVivo. Initially, 67 factors were identified through literature and expert input, reduced to 20 using PCA and subsequently validated through qualitative thematic analysis. Findings The analysis identified seven key themes encompassing operational, risk, supplier capability, financial, governance, technological and ethical dimensions of pharmaceutical supply chains. Operational factors such as delivery accuracy, availability of supplies and cold chain capabilities are fundamental to supply continuity and patient safety. Risk-related factors, including political instability and labour disruptions, significantly impact supply chain resilience. Supplier capabilities, governance factors, technological innovation and ethical considerations jointly drive resilience, sustainability and competitiveness. Research limitations/implications The current study contributes to supplier selection theory by combining PCA with qualitative thematic analysis, with a focus on operational, technological, governance and ethical aspects. The hybrid method of dimensionality reduction using machine learning and qualitative depth increases the reliability and interpretability of the data and understanding of the assessment processes for the healthcare supply chain. The framework also extends the humanitarian logistics literature by connecting commercial upstream supplier decisions to the preparedness and resilience of downstream health supply chains serving populations affected by disruptions and crises. Practical implications Healthcare organizations should adopt a multi-criteria approach to supplier evaluation, considering delivery accuracy, cold chain, financial sustainability and regulatory compliance, all of which affect patient safety and the continuity of essential medicines. Building resilient, health-system-aligned supply chains requires investment in digital technologies like AI, along with proactive measures such as multi-sourcing and geographic diversification. For humanitarian organizations, national procurement agencies and global health programmes, the prioritized factors provide a screening template for evaluating pharmaceutical suppliers whose reliability ultimately determines whether essential medicines reach crisis-affected and underserved populations. Originality/value This study contributes to the literature by providing a holistic, multi-dimensional framework that integrates PCA-based machine learning and NVivo-based qualitative insights for supplier selection – an approach not previously applied in the pharmaceutical supply chain context. It further contributes to the humanitarian logistics and health supply chain literature by demonstrating how upstream supplier selection functions as a preparedness mechanism for maintaining access to essential medicines under conditions of political instability, labour disruption and demand shocks.

summary: This study analyzes the relationship between digitalization, structural transformation, and carbon emission intensity in six ASEAN countries, namely Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam, and Cambodia. The study uses annual panel data for the period 2004–2024, with the main estimation period covering 2010–2024. Carbon emission intensity is used as the dependent variable, while the number of internet users, industry value added, urban population, GDP per capita, international trade, and services sector value added are used as independent variables. All variables are transformed into natural logarithms so that the coefficients can be interpreted as elasticities. Estimation is conducted using the Fixed Effects Model with period fixed effects and Panel EGLS with period weights following model selection tests. The results show that digitalization, proxied by the number of internet users, has a positive but statistically insignificant relationship with carbon emission intensity. In contrast, industry value added, urban population, GDP per capita, and international trade have positive and significant relationships. Services sector value added has a negative and significant relationship with carbon emission intensity. These findings indicate that structural transformation toward the services sector is associated with lower emission intensity, while industrial expansion, urbanization, economic growth, and trade are associated with increased carbon emission intensity in the countries examined.

title: From Environmental Investment to Green Innovation: Ecosystem Niche and Open Innovation in Corporate Green Transition
summary: Manufacturing firms face a persistent challenge in green transition: environmental spending does not automatically generate meaningful innovation. This study examines how environmental protection investment affects green innovation performance through a firm’s central niche in a green innovation ecosystem and whether open innovation changes these pathways. Using a balanced panel of 1054 Chinese A-share-listed manufacturing firms from 2016 to 2022 (7378 firm-year observations), we estimate firm and year fixed-effects models and conduct mediation, subgroup, and robustness analyses. Environmental protection investment is positively associated with green innovation performance. Central niche depth partially mediates this relationship, suggesting that sustained concentration in core green technologies helps firms convert environmental resources into innovation outcomes. Central niche diversity does not mediate the relationship in the full sample. Open innovation exerts a direct positive moderating effect on environmental protection investment and green innovation, and it can amplify the transformation of the innovation niche depth into green innovation. A sensitivity analysis excluding 2022 suggests a diversity-mediated effect among open innovators, although this evidence remains exploratory. The findings show that corporate green transition depends on investment intensity, technological positioning, and collaboration governance. This study extends research on sustainable strategy and organizational transition by linking environmental resource commitment, ecosystem positioning, and open innovation.

title: Value Relevance of Earnings, Book Value and Operating Cash Flows: Evidence from Listed Industrial Goods Companies in Nigeria
summary: This study examined the relationship between value relevance of earnings, book value and operating cash flows: evidence from listed industrial goods companies in Nigeria over the period 2015–2024. The study adopted an ex-post facto research design and utilised a balanced panel dataset comprising 120 firm-year observations from 12 listed industrial goods companies selected from a population of 15 firms on the Nigerian Exchange. Market Price Per Share (MPS) was used as the proxy for market value, while Earnings Per Share (EPS), Book Value Per Share (BVPS), and Cash Flow from Operations Per Share (CFFO) were examined as accounting information variables, with firm size included as a control variable. Data was obtained from audited annual reports, financial statements, NGX publications, company websites, and Securities and Exchange Commission records. The data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation analysis, diagnostic tests, and panel regression techniques using EViews. The descriptive results revealed substantial variations in market prices and accounting information across the sampled firms. Correlation analysis showed strong positive relationships between MPS and EPS (r = 0.8789), CFFO (r = 0.8701), and BVPS (r = 0.8189), while firm size exhibited a moderate positive correlation with MPS (r = 0.6123). The findings provide preliminary evidence that accounting information is relevant to the market valuation of listed industrial goods companies in Nigeria. The study recommends improved quality, transparency, and timeliness of financial reporting to enhance the usefulness of accounting information to investors and other capital-market participants.

title: Green Production Modes in Platform Supply Chains Under Eco-Label Policies: A Cost Structure Perspective
summary: This study investigates how heterogeneous green production modes affect operational decisions and welfare outcomes in platform-based supply chains under eco-label policies. We develop a model consisting of a manufacturer and a platform, in which the government sets a product green standard and provides a per-unit subsidy. We consider two representative green production modes: development-intensive green production (DIGP), characterized by fixed investment costs, and marginal cost-intensive green production (MIGP), characterized by variable production costs. Within a Stackelberg game framework, we derive the equilibrium pricing and commission decisions and compare the two modes in terms of the feasible operating region, profit distribution, and social welfare. We explicitly incorporate cost structure heterogeneity into the analysis and investigate its interaction with the platform commission mechanism and policy intervention. The results show that whether green costs enter pricing decisions as fixed investments or marginal costs systematically changes equilibrium outcomes through the double-markup relationship arising from the interaction between green production costs and platform commissions. Specifically, MIGP has a broader feasible operating region and generates relatively higher manufacturer profits, whereas platform profits are relatively insensitive to the choice of green production mode. Government subsidies play a nonlinear moderating role: MIGP generates higher social welfare at relatively low subsidy levels, whereas DIGP generates higher welfare at relatively high subsidy levels. The welfare-reversal threshold is jointly determined by the fixed-cost coefficient, variable-cost coefficient, and consumers’ green preferences. By incorporating cost structure heterogeneity into a platform-based analytical framework, this study contributes to the green supply chain literature by revealing how heterogeneous green production modes fundamentally alter operational decisions, profit distribution, and welfare outcomes under environmental regulation. The findings provide a theoretical basis for green operations mediated by platforms and offer practical guidance for designing effective eco-label and subsidy policies.

title: Resource-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Compact LLMs for Supply Chain Operations: A Hybrid QLoRA and RAG Approach
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) offer transformative potential for enterprise automation, particularly within the highly complex and data-dense environments of transportation, supply chain management, and intralogistics. However, deploying foundational models in these specialized domains frequently results in a critical failure mode: confident generative hallucinations regarding company-specific, highly proprietary operational protocols. Furthermore, adapting these massive models typically requires prohibitive computational resources, placing them fundamentally out of reach for regional distribution hubs and mid-sized enterprises constrained by strict hardware budgets. This paper investigates the hypothesis that a compact, instruction-tuned Small Language Model (SLM) can be aggressively fine-tuned and semantically grounded to provide highly accurate, factually bound supply chain support while operating entirely within the constraints of a single commodity GPU. This research presents the end-to-end development, optimization, and deployment of IndustryGPT, a highly specialized logistics LLM. We utilize a parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) strategy, specifically 4-bit Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation (QLoRA), to adapt the 1.1-billion parameter TinyLlama base model using a single 16 GB NVIDIA T4 GPU. To systematically eliminate hallucinations and ground the model in factual warehouse operations, we introduce a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture powered by a local FAISS vector database. This hybrid pipeline dynamically retrieves and injects exact standard operating procedures (SOPs) such as inbound packet scanning workflows, tallying reconciliations, and strict fleet maintenance protocols directly into the inference context window. We evaluate the model's performance on a custom hybrid corpus merging customer support dialogues with synthetic routing data, reporting substantial gains in both structural coherence and factual adherence. The system successfully demonstrates that merging domain-specific supervised fine-tuning with dense vector retrieval allows lightweight, edge-deployed models to achieve enterprise-grade accuracy. Finally, the architecture is deployed via a Gradio web interface, providing an interactive, zero-hallucination conversational agent tailored for localized logistics exception handling, proving that data sovereignty and advanced AI automation can coexist on localized commodity hardware.

title: The influence mechanism of firm green technology cooperation: a supply chain perspective with evidence from chinese cases
summary: To address growing environmental challenges, focal firms are increasingly pursuing green technology cooperation within their supply chains. However, limited research has yet proposed a theoretical framework for green technology cooperation among firms from the perspective of supply chain. This study employs a multiple-case study of four Chinese focal firms to construct a theoretical framework explaining the mechanism of green technology cooperation. By integrating Technology-Organisation-Environment (TOE) theory and institutional theory, this framework identifies the influencing factors about focal firms’ willingness to cooperate in green technology from three dimensions, i.e., macro environment, supply chain environment and organisational preparation. It further explains how this willingness translates into performance improvement through three pathways: goal matching, collaborative innovation, and risk sharing. This framework deconstructs the complexity of focal firms’ green technology cooperation behaviour, reveals the black box of the transformation from cooperation willingness to performance, and offers insights for enhancing green technology application across supply chains.

title: Building antifragile humanitarian supply chains: the role of transactive memory systems and big data analytics culture
summary: Purpose This study aims to investigate how big data analytics culture (BDAC) contributes to the development of antifragile humanitarian supply chains. Specifically, this study examines the mediating role of transactive memory systems (TMSs) and the moderating role of the frequency of natural disasters in the relationship between TMS and antifragility. Design/methodology/approach The authors collected 290 survey responses from key humanitarian professionals involved in disaster response operations. To test the proposed relationships among BDAC, TMS, antifragility and disaster frequency, the authors used Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Findings The results of this study reveal that BDAC enhances antifragility only when fact-based decision-making improves information credibility, member specialization and coordination, core manifestations of TMS. TMS fully mediates the relationship between BDAC and antifragility, while the positive effect of TMS on antifragility is stronger in contexts with frequent natural disasters. Originality/value This paper advances the literature by empirically demonstrating TMS as the underlying mechanism linking BDAC to antifragility in humanitarian supply chains, showing how TMS operate as microfoundations of dynamic capabilities that enable collective sensing, coordinated decision-making and the reconfiguration of practices.

title: Blind Box Cultural Marketing Strategies in the Digital Economy: A Case Study of POP MART
summary: Digital platforms have changed how people search for products, talk about brands and share their purchases. In the trendy toy market, this change is especially visible because buying a figure can involve character stories, online discussion and offline experience at the same time. This study examines POP MART as a case of blind box cultural marketing in the digital economy. A qualitative case study and literature analysis are used, drawing on academic research, POP MART's 2025 annual report and documented marketing practices. The analysis focuses on three dimensions: cultural marketing and brand value, digital platforms and consumer participation, and blind box consumption experience and brand loyalty. The findings suggest that POP MART builds value through character IP, keeps these characters visible through digital content and consumer sharing, and extends the blind box experience through collecting, communities and physical spaces. Although the blind box remains important, long term IP development and cultural adaptation appear more important for the future of the brand. The case may also be useful for other cultural consumption brands trying to build lasting consumer relationships.

title: Analysis of Sustainable Investment Strategies on Emerging Financial Markets in Nigeria
summary: This study examined the impact of sustainable investment strategies on emerging financial markets in Nigeria, with specific focus on the stock market. The study is motivated by the growing global emphasis on sustainability and the limited empirical evidence on how sustainability-oriented investments influence financial market development in emerging economies. Annual time series data covering the period from 1994 to 2025 were sourced from the Central Bank of Nigeria Statistical Bulletin and the OECD Climate Finance Database. Stock market capitalization was used as a proxy for emerging financial market performance, while sustainable investment strategies were captured through investment in climate financing, renewable energy measured by the percentage of electricity generated from renewable sources, agribusiness investment, and foreign direct investment. The study employed descriptive statistics and Ordinary Least Squares regression techniques to analyse the data. The findings reveal that investment in agribusinesses and renewable energy has positive and statistically significant effects on stock market capitalization, indicating that these forms of sustainable investment enhance market performance. Investment in climate financing shows a statistically significant but negative relationship with stock market performance, suggesting inefficiencies in the transmission of climate related funds to capital market activities. Foreign direct investment was found to have a negative and statistically insignificant effect on the stock market. The study concludes that sustainable investment strategies have differential effects on Nigeria’s emerging financial market and recommends policies that strengthen the integration of sustainability driven investments into the stock market framework to enhance long term market development.

title: Disaggregating ESG Practices and Performance Outcomes: Empirical Evidence From the European Healthcare Industry
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines the associations between Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) practices and organizational performance in 283 European hospitals. Drawing on agency theory, stakeholder theory, and the resource‐based view, it analyses ESG indicators as accounting‐relevant information within the institutional context of European healthcare. Using 2021 ESG scores and 2023 accounting and operational outcomes from ORBIS, the study applies PLS‐SEM to examine operating cash flow, profitability (ROA/ROE), and operational efficiency. In the baseline PLS‐SEM model, aggregate ESG is positively associated with all three outcomes, but disaggregation reveals substantial heterogeneity. Governance is positively associated with each outcome, social practices are negatively associated with profitability and operational efficiency, and environmental practices show no significant associations. The study contributes by showing that aggregate ESG scores can obscure pillar‐specific mechanisms and theoretically expected time horizons. In European healthcare, governance displays more direct accounting relevance, whereas the potential benefits of social and environmental practices may be indirect, non‐financial, or deferred.

title: Digital Transformation and Systemic Risk in Chinese Commercial Banks: Dynamic and Conditional-Effect Analyses
summary: Using an unbalanced panel of 200 Chinese commercial banks over 2010–2021, this study measures systemic risk using market-based marginal expected shortfall (MES) for listed banks and SVM-completed MES for non-listed banks. Two-way fixed-effects, distributed-lag, conditional-effect, heterogeneity, and endogeneity analyses indicate that overall digital transformation is associated with lower systemic risk. Strategic and management digitalization reduce risk, whereas business digitalization is associated with contemporaneous adjustment pressure. The negative effect of overall transformation emerges mainly in later periods, is stronger for banks with greater asset-side risk-bearing capacity, stronger interbank funding dependence, and lower profitability, and is more pronounced among nationwide banks than regional banks. The findings clarify how digital transformation can support banking-system stability while informing the balance between financial innovation and prudential regulation.

title: Internal Control over Financial Reporting in Lease Cycles under SOX 404
summary: Background: IFRS 16 and its Indonesian adoption through PSAK 73 bring most leases onto the statement of financial position, increasing the importance of reliable contract data and timely control execution in capital-intensive entities. Objective: This study examines the design and operating effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting (ICoFR) in the lease transaction cycle of a dual-listed infrastructure enterprise during the post-remediation stabilization phase. Methods: A descriptive qualitative single instrumental case study design was applied using a top-down, risk-based approach derived from PCAOB AS 2201. Evidence was triangulated through semi-structured interviews with six functionally diverse informants, guided observation, and inspection of five key control working papers covering 2023–2026. Results: All five key controls were adequately designed. However, operating effectiveness testing identified a control deficiency involving delayed lease modification updates and inconsistent data input by field business units. The deficiency did not escalate to a significant deficiency or material weakness because the K-02 compensating control consistently detected and corrected potential misstatements before the financial statements were issued. Conclusion: Reliable ICoFR in a decentralized lease cycle depends on both sound control design and timely first-line risk ownership. The findings support stronger data standardization, accountability for contract-change reporting, and proportionate, sustainable automation of upstream contract administration.

title: Cloud Accounting and Financial Performance of Manufacturing Firms in Nigeria: A Theoretical Perspective
summary: The rapid advancement of information and communication technology has transformed accounting practices globally. Cloud accounting has emerged as a modern accounting solution that enables organizations to access accounting information and financial data through internet based platforms. This theoretical article examines the relationship between cloud accounting and the financial performance of manufacturing firms in Nigeria. The study explores the conceptual foundations of cloud accounting, reviews relevant literature, and adopts the Technology Acceptance Theory (TAM) and Resource-Based View (RBV) Theory as the theoretical underpinning for analysis. The article argues that cloud accounting enhances operational efficiency, reduces costs, improves decision-making, strengthens financial reporting quality, and ultimately contributes to improved financial performance. The study concludes that the adoption of cloud accounting can provide manufacturing firms in Nigeria with a sustainable competitive advantage and recommends increased investment in cloud-based accounting technologies.

title: Preventing recurring material misstatements through behavioural sustainment: a 5S-based conceptual framework for financial reporting
summary: Purpose This paper develops a conceptual framework to explain how behavioural discipline is sustained in routine financial reporting work and how such sustainment conditions the recurrence of material misstatements under conditions of reasonable assurance. Rather than treating reporting reliability as an outcome optimised through technical rules or ex post detection, the paper reconceptualises financial reporting as a behaviourally enacted process shaped by routines, accountability, and reinforcement over time. Design/methodology/approach The paper adopts a structured conceptual integration of accounting, management control and behavioural literature. The 5S principles – Sort, Set in Order, Shine, Standardise and Sustain – are reinterpreted as a behavioural process framework that explicates how reporting routines are enacted, coordinated, scrutinised and reinforced across reporting cycles. The approach is conceptual in nature and does not constitute a systematic review or a design science intervention. Findings The framework suggests that the recurrence of material misstatements is shaped less by the presence of additional procedures than by the extent to which disciplined reporting practices are behaviourally sustained over time. It explicates how 5S operates through behavioural mechanisms – such as selective attention to materiality, anticipatory coordination, anomaly questioning, accountable judgement and reinforcement across cycles – that condition how formal reporting requirements are enacted in practice, without assuming the elimination of judgement or error. Research limitations/implications As a conceptual paper, the framework does not provide empirical evidence of effectiveness and is developed primarily from literature grounded in regulated reporting environments. Practical implications The paper offers accountants, auditors, boards and regulators a conceptual lens for interpreting whether reporting routines are behaviourally sustained or have become symbolic, without implying a prescriptive intervention. Originality/value The paper reframes misstatement prevention as a problem of behavioural sustainment rather than technical optimisation, enabling recurring reporting failures to be analysed as manifestations of instability in routine enactment rather than isolated procedural deficiencies.

title: Effect of Supply Chain Practices on Operational Performance of Manufacturing Companies in Rwanda: A Case of Bakhresa Grain Milling Rwanda Ltd
summary: The study assessed the effect of supply chain practices on operational performance at Bakhresa Grain Milling Rwanda Ltd, Rwanda, for the period.The specific objectives examined inventory management practices, transportation management practices, information flow management practices and warehousing management practices.The Theory of Constraints, Transaction Cost Economics Theory, Organizational Information Processing Theory and Resource-Based View guided the study by linking the four practices to product quality, customer satisfaction, cost minimization and profit maximization.A descriptive and correlational design was used with quantitative and qualitative approaches.The study population comprised 240 Bakhresa Grain Milling Rwanda Ltd employees, with 150 respondents selected through proportionate stratified sampling across six departments, followed by simple random sampling within each stratum.Questionnaire data were analyzed in SPSS version 29.Inventory management practices had a positive significant effect on operational performance (B = 0.198, t = 3.356, p = 0.001), transportation management practices also had a positive significant effect (B = 0.178, t = 2.543, p = 0.012), information flow management practices had the strongest positive effect (B = 0.353, t = 5.431, p = 0.000), and warehousing management practices produced a positive significant effect (B = 0.337, t = 5.912, p = 0.000).The model explained 90.4% of the variation in operational performance.The study concluded that accurate stock control, reliable transport, timely information and disciplined warehouse execution jointly strengthened operational performance.It recommended integrated demand forecasting, supplier coordination, route control, system integration and warehouse verification.

title: Audit committee diversity as a moderator of the relationship between financial crises and firm profitability: evidence from the COVID-19 pandemic
summary: Purpose This study examines the moderating role of audit committee diversity in the nexus between financial crises (the COVID-19 crisis) and profitability. Design/methodology/approach This study analyses Jordanian non-financial companies listed on the Amman Stock Exchange as a sample for the study from 2018 to 2022. The hypotheses were tested using panel-corrected standard errors (PCSE) regression analysis to address the issues of heteroscedasticity and autocorrelation. This study uses the system Generalised Method of Moments (GMM), along with fixed-effects and dynamic regression analyses to address endogeneity concerns. Findings This paper concluded that the COVID-19 crisis negatively impacted the profitability of companies. Gender diversity moderated this relationship, significantly mitigating the negative impact of the pandemic, whereas the results did not indicate that nationality diversity played a moderating role. Practical implications This investigation relies on the novel results concerning the moderating effects of audit committee diversity characteristics, offering guidance to regulators on incorporating these underrepresented traits into corporate governance codes in Jordan and similar developing countries. Originality/value The literature investigating diversity’s influence on corporate profitability during crises predominantly emphasizes board-level diversity, direct impacts, and gender diversity. However, it often overlooks diversity within the audit committee and its effects when interacting with a crisis. To the author’s knowledge, this is the first study examining the moderating role of audit committee diversity (gender and nationality) in the association between the COVID-19 crisis and profitability in developing countries.

title: Digital Transformation in Metallurgical Sector Logistics: A Case Study on the BPM Life Cycle of the Delivery Process Area
summary: The metallurgical sector faces significant logistic challenges to achieve efficient deliveries and increase customer satisfaction. This study analyzes and evaluates the application of the Business Process Management life cycle in the delivery process of a metallurgical company. Observation techniques, interviews, and surveys were used with clients as key actors in the process to evaluate the current logistics situation. Based on the evaluation outcomes, strategies and tools were identified to optimize planning, monitoring, and communication in the delivery process through the implementation of software for route optimization and order tracking in real time. Project management was developed under the Project Management Body of Knowledge methodological framework, which guaranteed efficient implementation and control. The results show significant improvements in operations and customer experience. This outcome emphasizes the importance of the digitalization of logistics to meet the specific demands and efficiency requirements of the metallurgical sector.

title: Green Innovation Effects and Driving Factors of Urban Environmental Information Disclosure: Based on fsQCA and Complex Mediation Analysis
summary: Abstract Government environmental information disclosure (Pollution Information Transparency Index, PITI) is a critical step in the environmental management system. To investigate the key elements driving government environmental information disclosure in a complex environment, this study uses sample data from 120 prefecture-level cities in China and employs the Pollution Source Regulatory Information Transparency Index to measure this disclosure. Based on the push–pull–mooring model, it utilizes fuzzy set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) and a mixed mediating effect model to analyze the configurational pathways influenced by factors such as public environmental demands, regional environmental problems, fiscal pressure, government–enterprise relationships, the rule of law environment, and governmental environmental attentiveness that facilitate high levels of government environmental information disclosure (PITI). Furthermore, it examines the direct and indirect effects of these configurations on regional green innovation. The findings reveal that six push–pull–mooring factors yield four conditional configurations for government environmental information disclosure. Overall, high public environmental demands and low fiscal pressure are universal conditions that drive government environmental information disclosure. Additionally, the complex mediating effect analysis shows that all four configurations can directly promote regional green innovation and also indirectly enhance it by fostering PITI. This paper thoroughly explores the underlying mechanisms by which different configurational pathways influence regional green innovation and systematically analyzes the interactions among various factors, providing new insights for advancing governmental transparency and offering theoretical guidance and practical recommendations for promoting regional green development.

title: Measuring Business Value from Enterprise Analytics: Ethical Tensions, Valuation Frameworks, and Stakeholder Reconciliation
summary: The value of enterprise analytics has become a strategic necessity for today’s organizations, but the perception of business value is conceptually scattered and ethically debatable. The critical juncture between value measurement systems and ethical governance practices in enterprise analytics is explored through a comparison of purely financial return-on-investment (ROI) value frameworks and multi-stakeholder value frameworks, examining how they shape organizational decision-making and ethical outcomes. The study’s conceptual reconciliation process is grounded in a literature review of four key theories stakeholder theory, algorithmic fairness, integrated reporting, and data governance and identifies four fundamental ethical tensions: (1) shareholder primacy versus broader stakeholder equity; (2) short-term financial metrics versus long-term sustainability value; (3) algorithmic fairness versus analytical efficiency; and (4) opacity of data-driven decisions versus transparency obligations. The paper proposes a multi-dimensional value architecture combining financial performance indicators, environmental, social and governance (ESG) indicators, stakeholder participation mechanisms, and ethical audit procedures. The analysis suggests that organizations implementing stakeholder-inclusive analytics frameworks realize greater trust, innovation potential, and long-term resilience than those relying on financial ROI logic alone. The proposed framework is theoretically significant in extending stakeholder theory to the analytics domain, and practically significant in offering governance tools for reconciling conflicting value claims without compromising stakeholder rights or fairness. Policy implications for corporate governance boards and analytics practitioners are discussed.

title: GENDER DIVERSITY IN TOP MANAGEMENT AND CORPORATE VALUE CREATION: EVIDENCE FROM CORPORATE BOARDS IN COLOMBIA.
summary: Background Gender diversity in corporate governance has gained increasing relevance due to regulatory changes, investor expectations, and its potential contribution to strategic decision-making and corporate value creation. Despite recent progress, women remain underrepresented on corporate boards. This study analyzes the relationship between female board participation and the financial performance of publicly traded companies in Colombia. Methods A quantitative, descriptive, and explanatory approach was employed. The study focused on Colombian publicly traded companies, particularly those included in the COLCAP index. Board composition and female participation were characterized using corporate and bibliographic sources, while financial and ESG data were obtained from LSEG and Refinitiv. Regression models examined the relationship between female board participation and financial performance, measured through ROA, and ROE, controlling for sales and ESG performance. Results Female participation on corporate boards increased substantially between 2015 and 2024, although significant differences remain across firms and sectors. The energy sector showed comparatively higher levels of female representation. Econometric results indicate a positive and statistically significant relationship between female board participation and ROE, with a correlation coefficient of 0.807 and a coefficient of determination of 65.1%, significant at the 1% level. These findings suggest that gender diversity is associated with improved corporate profitability. Conclusions Female participation on corporate boards is positively associated with financial performance, particularly ROE. Greater gender diversity may strengthen strategic decision-making and contribute to corporate value creation. However, persistent differences across firms and limited female representation in top governance positions indicate that further institutional and corporate efforts are required to achieve substantive gender equality.

title: Integrating hesitant fuzzy linguistic term sets with ordinal priority approach: Application to digital supply chain supplier selection
summary: Background Multi-criteria decision making problems often involve multiple decision makers who express their preferences using imprecise linguistic terms rather than exact numerical values. The Ordinal Priority Approach (OPA) derives weights directly from ordinal preferences, but its standard form assumes crisp ranks and cannot capture hesitancy. Methodology This paper proposes a Hesitant Fuzzy Linguistic Term Set based Ordinal Priority Approach (HFLTS-OPA) for supplier selection in digital supply chains. Comparative linguistic expressions are converted into ordinal rank intervals and used to build a dual-bound OPA model whose paired optimistic and pessimistic programs yield interval priorities, ranked by possibility degree and non-dominance. The method is demonstrated on a manufacturing case with 3 decision makers, 8 criteria, and 10 suppliers. Findings Cost emerged as the dominant criterion, followed by quality and by information sharing and digital collaboration, confirming the growing importance of digital capabilities alongside conventional sourcing priorities. The method produced a clear supplier ordering that remained stable across all tested weight-sum ranges, and six HFLTS-based benchmark methods converged on the same leading alternatives. Originality The study is the first to integrate hesitant comparative linguistic expressions with OPA, preserving hesitation through to interval-valued priorities without pairwise comparisons or normalization.

title: Do sovereign ratings capture public pension liabilities in the assessment of public debt? A France–UK comparison
summary: IMPACTThis article is intended primarily for investors, rating agencies and credit analysts assessing sovereign solvency. Its analysis may also be relevant to finance ministries, audit institutions, parliamentarians, fiscal authorities and public sector accountants. The article’s message is practical: pension liabilities are an important factor affecting sovereign solvency and should be given more weight by credit rating agencies (CRAs). The main difficulty lies in differences in pension systems and accounting methods across countries. The authors propose focusing on states’ income statements presented in financial reports under accrual accounting standards. Official debt must remain the central indicator, but it should not be read alone.
