title: Two hands of green innovation: how digital social responsibility fuels circular economy practices and net-zero outcomes
summary: Purpose This study investigates how digital social responsibility contributes to sustainability transformation by examining its effects on green innovation, circular economy practices, and net-zero-based green performance. Drawing on Stakeholder Theory and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the study explores the mechanisms through which digitally enabled responsibility shapes innovation-based environmental outcomes. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research design is employed, using survey data collected from technology-based firms in Vietnam. Structural equation modeling is applied to test the proposed relationships among digital social responsibility, exploitative and exploratory green innovation, circular economy practices, and net-zero-based green performance. Findings The results indicate that digital social responsibility is positively associated with exploratory green innovation but not with exploitative green innovation. Exploratory green innovation is positively associated with circular economy practices, and both green innovation and circular economy practices are positively associated with net-zero-based green performance. In addition, digital social responsibility shows significant positive associations with both circular economy practices and net-zero-based green performance. Originality/value This study advances digital sustainability literature by redefining digital social responsibility as a digital sustainability orchestration capability that links stakeholder engagement with dynamic capability formation. It further reveals how digital social responsibility-driven exploratory innovation translates into circular-economy practices and net-zero-based green performance in emerging-economy technology firms, offering new process-level insights into the digital-enabled sustainability transformation.

title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION MANAGEMENT IN ISLAMIC EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS: ADAPTATION STRATEGIES FOR THE ERA OF THE INDUSTRIAL REVOLUTION 4.0 AND 5.0
summary: Digital transformation is both a challenge and an opportunity for Islamic educational institutions in facing the dynamics of the Industrial Revolution 4.0 and Society 5.0. This study aims to analyze the digital transformation management strategies implemented by Islamic educational institutions in improving the effectiveness of governance and learning quality. The research method used is a qualitative approach with the library research method, which is by examining various literature and the latest research results that are relevant to the topic of digital transformation and Islamic education management. The results of the study show that the success of digital transformation is determined by three main aspects, namely visionary leadership based on Islamic values, strengthening the digital literacy of educators and education personnel, and integrating information technology systems in the management of educational institutions. In addition, it was found that Islamic educational institutions that are able to adapt strategically to technological changes have higher competitiveness in creating an effective, innovative, and characterful learning ecosystem. The conclusion of this study emphasizes the importance of synergy between spiritual values and technological innovation in realizing globally competitive Islamic education in the digital era.

title: Three‐buffy‐coat platelet concentrates: Evaluation of a Welsh blood supply chain contingency strategy with wider opportunities for European practice
summary: Abstract Background and Objectives Platelet concentrates (PC) are essential for haemostatic support in clinical care. The Welsh Blood Service (WBS) previously showed through data modelling that three‐buffy‐coat‐derived PC (3BC‐PC) could meet UK contingency and European Directorate for the Quality of Medicines & HealthCare (EDQM) Council of Europe specifications. This study aimed to validate the real‐world manufacture of 3BC‐PC, assessing quality and compliance against UK and European regulatory standards. Materials and Methods Three ABO ‐compatible BCs were pooled with platelet additive solution‐E ( PAS ‐E) and processed per standard WBS protocols. Sixteen 3BC ‐ PC were manufactured and stored at 20–24°C with agitation for 7 days. Samples were tested on Days 1, 2, 6 and 8 for platelet yield, recovery and specification compliance. Functional and quality assessments included platelet activation ( CD62P , Annexin V, soluble CD62P ), biochemistry ( pH , glucose, lactate), light transmission aggregometry (adenosine diphosphate [ ADP] , thrombin receptor activator peptide‐6 [ TRAP ‐6]) and thromboelastography (TEG) (R, K, α‐angle, maximum amplitude [ MA] ). Results Mean platelet yield was 247 ± 26 × 10 9 /unit following Day 2 bacteriology sampling. All 3BC‐PC met UK contingency (≥150 × 10 9 /unit) and EDQM routine (≥200 × 10 9 /unit) specifications throughout storage, although UK routine compliance (≥240 × 10 9 /unit) declined to 62.5% following Day 2 bacteriology sampling. Biochemical, activation and functional changes reflected expected platelet storage lesions, while TEG showed preserved global haemostatic function. Conclusion Practical validation supports the feasibility of 3BC‐PC as a contingency component. Quality metrics aligned with UK and European specifications, suggesting operational and clinical viability. These findings bridge prior modelling with practical manufacture and support both UK contingency and routine European adoption while identifying future optimisation considerations for potential routine UK use.

title: Strategi Peningkatan Sustainable Supply Chain Performance Pada Perusahaan Remanufaktur Melalui Sustainable Value Stream Mapping (Sus-VSM)
summary: Persaingan global memerlukan strategi yang tidak hanya bertumpu pada efisiensi, tetapi juga harus memperhatikan aspek lingkungan. Remanufaktur sebagai bagian dari ekonomi sirkular menjadi solusi strategis melalui pengurangan limbah, penghematan sumber daya dan pelestarian nilai produk. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengevaluasi kinerja SSCM di PT Komatsu Remanufacturing Asia (P.T KRA) menggunakan metode Sustainable Value Stream Mapping (Sus-VSM) yang terintegrasi dengan Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP). Untuk memastikan proses penelitian didukung oleh data yang valid, maka pada penelitian ini pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui observasi langsung, wawancara, serta pengumpulan data primer dan sekunder. Perancangan Metrik pengukuran keberlanjutan dikembangkan berdasarkan kajian literatur dan divalidasi menggunakan pengujian konstansi, validitas dan reliabilitas. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kinerja SSCM perusahaan P.T KRA berada pada kategori cukup baik (Moderately Good) dengan nilai indeks keberlanjutan sebesar 77. Dimensi lingkungan dan sosial menunjukkan kinerja yang relatif kuat, akan tetapi dimensi ekonomi masih memerlukan perbaikan, khususnya pada pengurangan lead time, peningkatan overall equipment effectiveness (OEE), efisiensi penggunaan air dan pengelolaan limbah padat. Temuan ini menegaskan pentingnya Sus-VSM sebagai alat evaluasi komprehensif untuk mendukung peningkatan efisiensi secara berkelanjutan dalam rantai pasok remanufaktur.

title: From Accounting Records to Actionable Insights: Developing Business Analytics Capability in Small Enterprises
summary: Small enterprises may possess accounting records and digital dashboards without a reliable process for converting information into business decisions. This article examines that conversion through a focused narrative review of nine research and institutional sources concerning financial practices, analytics adoption, organisational capability and analytical reasoning. The synthesis distinguishes experimental effects from observational associations, policy evidence and stakeholder perceptions. It proposes an accounting to action framework linking a defined decision, dependable records, purpose appropriate analysis, understandable interpretation, documented action and subsequent review. The central proposition is that interpretation and review should be assessed alongside technology access: owners should be able to explain what an output supports, what it leaves uncertain and why a particular action follows. A worked hypothetical example demonstrates how revenue growth can coexist with a cash constraint. Implications for Bangladesh emphasise locally adapted instruction and evaluation rather than assumed transfer of foreign results. The framework is conceptual, not empirically validated. Its contribution is an operational account of how accounting discipline and learning routines can support business analytics, together with testable propositions and a design for evaluating decision quality separately from enterprise performance.Keywords: accounting information; business analytics; small enterprises; digital transformation; decision quality; Bangladesh

title: Measuring Climate Risk Spillovers for Sustainable Finance: A Quantile Time-Frequency Multilayer Network Analysis of Carbon, Energy, and Metals Markets
summary: Global warming has made climate physical and transition risks systemic sources of financial instability and key challenges to sustainability. These risks can spread to carbon, energy, and metals markets, which are central to the low-carbon transition and sustainable finance. This paper, therefore, explores the Quantile Time-Frequency connections among climate physical risk, climate transition risk, and the carbon, energy, and metals markets, with the analysis conducted through the lens of higher-moment risks. Using climate physical and transition risk indices together with daily carbon, energy, and metals futures settlement prices spanning 1 July 2015 to 29 December 2023, we employ the GJRSK model to extract higher-moment risk measures and apply the Quantile Time-Frequency framework to examine spillover effects across return, volatility, skewness, and kurtosis dimensions under different quantiles over the short term and long term. Furthermore, we construct a multilayer network that integrates information on return, volatility, skewness, and kurtosis risks under diverse market conditions and measure the topological properties of this network. The results reveal the following key insights: First, higher-moment risk spillovers are pronounced, though their magnitude is lower than that of return and volatility spillovers. Second, return, skewness, and kurtosis spillovers are primarily short-term driven, while volatility spillovers are concentrated in the long run. Climate risks generally act as receivers, but they shift to transmitters during long-term market downturns. Finally, findings from the multilayer complex network analysis demonstrate pronounced differences in the structural configurations of the interconnected networks linking climate risks to the return, volatility, skewness, and kurtosis risks of the carbon, energy, and metals markets across varying conditional quantiles. These findings support the measurement and monitoring of climate-related systemic risk and provide implications for sustainable finance, carbon and energy transition policies, and cross-market risk governance.

title: The Impact of Sustainability Reporting on Directors' ESG Duties: The Disclosure-Duty Feedback Loop
summary: Maturation of sustainability reporting has expanded, rather than resolved, the ambiguity surrounding directors’ ESG duties. Reporting standards specify what must be disclosed, but not what directors must do behind the disclosure, while regulatory regimes diverge in scope, materiality and enforcement. The paper explains this paradox through a “disclosure-duty feedback loop”. Because company law regulates process rather than outcomes, mandatory reporting requires boards to establish and oversee systems capable of producing reliable disclosures, drawing them into the governance of the underlying subject matter. Each report then becomes a benchmark against which subsequent board conduct may be assessed, causing the obligation to ratchet upward as disclosure becomes mandatory and assured. The paper traces this loop across three regimes: an ISSB baseline adopted in Singapore and the United Kingdom; an EU regime narrowed by Omnibus I but retaining a commitment to double materiality; and a US regime withdrawn at the federal level, while California extends reporting obligations extraterritorially. It shows that the loop operates through existing duties, with three channels in the United Kingdom, two in Singapore and effectively one in Delaware. The loop therefore inherits the limits of those duties in standard, foreseeability and enforcement, and is strained where listing and incorporation jurisdictions diverge. It strengthens monitoring without making directors guarantors of ESG outcomes. The paper proposes four reforms: clearer oversight duties, safe harbours for good-faith forward-looking and Scope 3 disclosures, proportionate assurance, and mutual recognition for dual reporters.

title: Corporate Sustainability and Executive Equity Incentives: Evidence from ESG Disclosure Quality in China
summary: Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosure is increasingly important for corporate sustainability, yet less is known about how internal incentive arrangements shape firms’ sustainability transparency. This study examines changes in ESG disclosure quality following executive equity incentive plan adoption among Chinese A-share listed firms from 2010 to 2024. We employ a propensity-score-matched difference-in-differences (PSM-DID) design to compare firms adopting equity incentive plans with similar firms that remain untreated. The results show that ESG disclosure quality increases significantly following plan adoption, and the main finding remains robust across multiple robustness checks, including estimators that account for staggered treatment timing. The improvement extends across environmental, social, and governance disclosure, with the strongest response in the environmental dimension. Mechanism analysis provides evidence consistent with reduced managerial myopia as a partial channel. Further analyses show larger point estimates for longer contractual horizons, mature firms, and firms in polluting industries, although only the life-cycle difference is marginally significant. Overall, the findings suggest that executive equity incentives are associated with greater sustainability transparency, consistent with the view that incentive design can shape managerial decision horizons and disclosure behavior.

title: Business Structure and Environmental Sustainability Strategy in China's EV Battery Industry: A Comparative Case Study of CATL and BYD
summary: This study examines how business structure shapes the design and implementation of environmental sustainability strategies in China's EV-battery industry by comparing CATL, a specialised battery supplier, with BYD, a vertically integrated battery-and-vehicle producer. Using a qualitative comparative case-study design, it analyses corporate ESG and annual reports, official policy documents, academic literature and market-share data from 2023 to mid-2025. Drawing on sustainable supply chain management, global value-chain governance and the natural-resource-based view, the analysis identifies two overlapping coordination pathways. CATL's model is associated with more formalised inter-organisational carbon governance, supplier coordination and product-footprint accounting. BYD's integration supports closer links among battery-vehicle design, manufacturing efficiency and internal energy management, while still requiring upstream supplier governance. Market leadership can amplify implementation capacity but does not measure sustainability. The study shows that organisational boundaries shape where sustainability decisions and capabilities are coordinated across the value chain.

title: Forecasting Product Demand and PET Bottle Return Flows in Closed Loop Supply Chains: A Hybrid Machine Learning Approach for Emerging Markets
summary: This study examined whether monthly demand and PET bottle return forecasts improve planning in a closed-loop beverage network in Nigeria. The analysis covers Coke, Fanta, Sprite, Big Cola, and Eva from 2019 to 2024, combining product observations with variables calibrated from the underlying network study. We compare XGBoost, random forest, support vector regression, and long short-term memory (LSTM) with the moment-matching benchmark. Model selection and testing preserve temporal order. XGBoost records the lowest point forecast errors for the five products, reducing average demand mean absolute percentage error from 14.6 to 9.8 percent. For returns, its prediction interval coverage is 78 to 84 percent against a nominal 80 percent, compared with 50 to 62 percent for moment matching. SHAP analysis assigns the largest demand contributions to recent sales, seasonality, and temperature; recovery rate, collection coverage, and reverse logistics cost are prominent for returns. We then use the forecasts in the network optimisation model, retaining its structure and cost coefficients. Expected cost falls by 12 to 18 percent across the tested configurations. The XGBoost and LSTM ensemble gives the largest saving, ₦25.977 million. These results concern the studied network and its calibrated inputs. They support evaluating forecasts through their planning consequences as well as prediction error, with external validation needed before the simulated savings are applied to other networks.

title: Climate Risk in ESG Portfolios: Evidence from Indonesian Equity Markets
summary: We examine climate variables in a pipeline for dynamic Value-at-Risk (VaR) of the SRI-KEHATI ESG index and the IHSG (Jakarta Composite Index). Using 1,499 daily observations (20142025), we combine the Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) over 50 candidate predictors, a quantile regression neural network (QRNN) for VaR at three quantile levels, and SHAP for attribution. LASSO removes all climate variables from both indices. For IHSG, the partial correlation of clean-energy returns falls from 0.121 to 0.0005 once domestic equity factors enter, consistent with domestic absorption, though constituent overlap cannot exclude a purely compositional explanation. A diagnostic quantile regression shows climate contributions rising 2.82-fold from VaR 90% to VaR 99%, but the pattern is flat under the QRNN itself (ratio 1.03). In the main backtest, QRNN has lower pinball loss than Historical Simulation and GARCH(1,1)-t in all 12 DieboldMariano comparisons (p 0.001), although it uses same-day predictors the benchmarks lack and the advantage was not reproduced in the ablation. In a common-sample ablation (n = 249 of 300 nominal test days), LASSO pre-selection is associated with 4 of 6 Kupiec passes versus 0 of 6 without it, but IHSG still fails at two of three quantile levels. Whether SRI-KEHATI screening isolates climate risk was not tested; mediation covers IHSG only.

title: Compliance or Commitment? Hindustan Unilever's CSR Practice Under India's Mandatory CSR Regime, FY 2020-21 to FY 2024-25
summary: This paper examines Hindustan Unilever Limited’s (HUL) corporate social responsibility practice under Section 135 of India’s Companies Act, 2013. It uses a single-case design, drawing on HUL’s disclosed CSR financial data for FY 2020–21 to FY 2024–25, national CSR data, programme reports and peer-reviewed research. It examines how HUL’s spending compares with its statutory obligation, how its CSR is governed and connected to business strategy, what outcomes its flagship programmes report, and what limits CSR’s reach, particularly in relation to plastic packaging. Three findings emerge. First, HUL spent 2.01%–2.04% of average net profit on CSR in each year examined, close to the statutory 2% threshold; its CSR spending grew by about 54% over the period, largely alongside profit growth. Second, the case suggests a distinction between compliance in spending and commitment in programme design: initiatives such as Project Shakti and the Hindustan Unilever Foundation’s water programmes are linked to the company’s distribution and supply-chain context. However, the strength of evidence for reported outcomes varies, and company disclosures are not equivalent to independent impact evaluation. Third, plastic packaging highlights the limits of community CSR where impacts are tied to wider business operations and regulatory obligations. The paper argues that CSR should be assessed not only by expenditure but also by strategic integration, the strength of outcome evidence and transparency about limitations. It proposes a practical framework for measuring CSR performance beyond compliance reporting. Preprint; not peer-reviewed.

title: K-REAP Digital Transformation: A Kerala Model for Sustainable Enterprise Resource Planning in Large-scale Higher Education Systems
summary: Digital transformation has become a strategic priority for higher education systems worldwide, yet large-scale enterprise resource planning (ERP) implementation remains one of the most challenging institutional reforms. Universities differ substantially in governance structures, academic regulations, examination processes, financial management systems and administrative workflows, complicating the deployment of a unified ERP. Kerala’s Resources for Educational Administration and Planning (K-REAP) project provides a unique opportunity to examine various ERP implementation models over more than a decade of policy experimentation. This article analyzes the evolution of ERP development strategies adopted in Kerala between 2013 and 2026, identifying the factors influencing their success and failure. Four implementation models are examined: centralized software development, integration of existing university applications, institution-owned ERP systems and software-as-a-service (SaaS)-based configurable ERP architecture implemented through K-REAP. Drawing on implementation experience across multiple universities, the study argues that a cloud-hosted, configurable SaaS architecture—supported by multi-level governance, centralized project management, distributed technical teams and vendor-supported continuous customization—offers a more sustainable approach than institution-owned ERP systems. The article proposes a higher education ERP deployment framework that may serve as a reference model for higher education systems implementing digital transformation at scale.

summary: The article provides a systematic critical analysis and a fundamental comprehensive assessment of the modern architecture of motivation models for top management of entities in the public sector of the economy of Ukraine in the context of macroeconomic instability, deepening structural transformations and challenges of post-war recovery. The specifics and dialectics of the functioning of compensation packages are analyzed in detail through the conceptual prism of the classical and neo-institutional theory of agency relations (Agency Theory), the concept of stakeholder capitalism (Stakeholder Capitalism). An analysis of European corporate governance practices is carried out (in particular, on the example of Equinor ASA, Norway). Based on the analysis, a comprehensive approach to adapting the best EU directives and recommendations to the domestic institutional landscape is developed, which forms a scientifically sound basis for reforming the strategic motivation of top management as a driver of the sustainability of the national economy. The key institutional and structural-organizational destructors of domestic corporate governance practice have been identified and systematically analyzed. In particular, the phenomenon of regulatory dualism in the public sector has been identified, which is caused by a constant regulatory gap between market requirements for attracting highly qualified leaders and strict directive restrictions on maximum remuneration levels (cap limits), fragmentation of corporate autonomy. A well-founded conclusion has been formulated that the public corporate sector is experiencing a critical devaluation and dysfunction of classical market instruments of long-term material incentives, which is due to strict regulation of the relevant relations. General conclusions are formulated based on the results of the study, in particular, the need for further implementation of OECD standards and EU directives (CSRD, CSDDD), which provide for the transition to a three-component remuneration structure with the dominance of long-term incentives (LTI), mandatory integration of non-financial ESG indicators, and legislative consolidation of bonus return mechanisms (Clawback), is substantiated.

title: The scent of ESG – climate change and environmental degradation in credit risk management
summary: How do credit risk managers respond to regulatory demands to integrate environmental, social, and governance-related (ESG) factors – especially climate change and environmental degradation – into credit risk management? Drawing on interviews with credit risk managers, this study presents two different ‘styles’ of risk assessment: The ‘explicit calculation’ approach aims to identify potential financial risks associated with climate change and environmental degradation through quantitative calculation and model-based analysis; ‘tacit judgment’ refers to certain intuitive ways of judgment, based on tacit knowledge, enabling the risk manager to assess ESG factors, without the need for quantification and calculation. While ‘explicit calculation’ offers communicable outputs demanded by regulators, it often fails to capture the indeterminate nature of ESG risks; ‘tacit judgment,’ though epistemically valuable, struggles for legitimacy because its tacit competencies resist codification. The analysis highlights these organizational and epistemic challenges that arise when climate change and environmental degradation are assessed for financial risks and underscores the critical role of tacit knowledge in contemporary credit risk management.

title: Compliance without Commitment? Mandatory ESG Reporting on the Mongolian Stock Exchange
summary: Stock exchanges in frontier markets increasingly require listed companies to publish environmental, social and governance (ESG) reports, yet little is known about whether such rules change how many firms report, when they report and what they file. This study evaluates the rule of the Mongolian Stock Exchange that, from October 2024, made annual ESG reporting mandatory for issuers in its top listing tier (Tier I) and left it voluntary in Tiers II and III. Using only public exchange records, we reconstruct each issuer's tier at every reporting deadline from the exchange's tier notices and date all 99 documents in its ESG registry, which yields 668 firm-years for 176 listed equities over the financial years 2022–2025. Difference-in-differences estimates with firm and year fixed effects, bias-reduced cluster-robust and wild cluster bootstrap inference show that the mandate raised the probability that a Tier I issuer posted an ESG report within five months of the deadline by 46 percentage points and the probability of posting by the 30 April deadline by 25 points. Tier I reporting was already rising before the rule, but among issuers that had never reported, the annual rate of starting rose from 26% to 78% in Tier I and from 1% to 3% elsewhere. Reporting followed the obligation rather than a commitment: two issuers moved out of Tier I in September 2025 stopped reporting, two moved into it started, and after the rule non-mandated issuers followed a report with another in only 5 of 11 cases, against 32 of 33 cases among mandated issuers. Compliance was partial and thin. Only 53% of mandated firm-years met the deadline, first reports produced under the mandate were shorter than those of earlier reporters (median 7 against 10 pages) and less often on time, about half of the posted documents are scanned images without machine-readable text, and six are in English. A tier-based mandate closed most of the reporting gap within two years, but exchanges need enforced deadlines and data standards to turn filings into information investors can use.

title: Knowledge‐Driven Supply Chain Digitalization and Fully Automated Baggage Handling System Success: The Mediating Role of Knowledge Integration Capability and the Moderating Role of Organizational Digital Readiness
summary: ABSTRACT The growing use of intelligent digital technologies is reshaping airport supply chains, but technology adoption alone does not explain why automated baggage handling initiatives succeed. knowledge‐driven supply chain digitalization (KSCD) is defined here as the organizational capability to use connected digital technologies and real‐time data to share information, coordinate decisions, and integrate baggage‐handling activities across airport supply‐chain actors. Fully Automated Baggage Handling System Success (FABHSS) is conceptualized as a multidimensional operational outcome reflected in efficiency, timely and reliable processing, routing accuracy and traceability, cross‐functional coordination, and overall support for baggage operations. Drawing on the Knowledge‐Based View and Dynamic Capability Theory (DCT), the study tested a moderated mediation model using survey data from 220 employees in airport operations, logistics, information technology, engineering, and baggage handling at major international airports in the United Arab Emirates. Covariance‐based structural equation modelling showed that KSCD positively influenced Knowledge Integration Capability (KIC; beta = 0.724, p < 0.001) and FABHSS (beta = 0.321, p < 0.001), while KIC positively influenced FABHSS (beta = 0.486, p < 0.001). Bootstrapping confirmed that KIC partially mediates the relationship between KSCD and FABHSS (indirect beta = 0.352, p < 0.001), and Organizational Digital Readiness strengthened the positive KSCD–KIC relationship (interaction beta = 0.184, p < 0.001). The findings show that automated baggage‐handling success depends on converting digitally generated information into integrated operational knowledge within a digitally ready organization.

title: The Law of Sequencing Coupling: The First Principles and Physical Turn of Supply Chain Management——On the Genesis Mechanism and Orthogonal Governance of "Mathematically Feasible, Yet Physically Inexecutable"
summary: For three decades, global manufacturing has invested hundreds of billions of dollars in supply chain digitalization, yet remains trapped in high inventory, late deliveries, and cross-functional KPI frictions. Traditional management science blames organizational misalignment, but this paper, derived from first principles of physics, delivers a counter-intuitive verdict: It is not KPI Conflict, it is KPI Coupling. Conflicts can be coordinated, but coupling cannot be decoupled; it can only be orthogonalized. 【Core Discovery & Academic Significance】This paper formally establishes Meng's Law of Sequencing Coupling.It reveals the axiomatic failure of traditional Operations Research reductionism (IID assumptions, additive scalar objectives, decomposable constraints). By constructing a minimal deterministic spatiotemporal model under "Four Sterile Baseline Hypotheses", the paper proves that even with 100% forecast accuracy, 100% clean data, and 100% constraint mapping, as long as planning requires sequencing, shared resources will inevitably undergo rigid topological coupling. This generates a Spatiotemporal Phase Cross-Mismatch, projecting onto the organizational boundary as Vector Cancellation, making a schedule mathematically feasible but physically inexecutable (Systemic Sudden Death). This means: any attempt to bypass this Law through algorithm optimization, S&OP alignment meetings, or brute-force AI scheduling models is essentially accelerating internal entropy generation and self-destruction. 【Solution & Industrial Validation】The only path to resolution is "coupling cannot be decoupled, it can only be orthogonally lifted." This paper establishes a Dual-Stage Orthogonal Governance Architecture: Extensive Material Stream Temporal Pull [O(N)] + Discrete Capacity Local Residual Permutation.This architecture has been validated in Lenovo Global Supply Chain, a mega-scale industrial complex with millions of discrete orders and hundreds of thousands of BOM levels. It has operated continuously and stably for 18 years, elevating the delivery commitment response rate to over 98%. 【Copyright & Patent Boundary】The theoretical framework is open-sourced globally under CC BY 4.0. However, engineering implementations—including the Living State Model, dual-helix orthogonal operators, and the IPC Engine—are strictly protected by multiple invention patents. Any commercial implementation requires formal written authorization from the patent holder. title: Geography-Based Funding and the Fintech Securities Crowdfunding Ecosystem in Indonesia: A Mixed-Method Analysis
summary: Background: The Fintech Securities Crowdfunding (SCF) industry in Indonesia has shown rapid growth, yet it faces challenges regarding the uneven distribution of funding access and the maturity of its ecosystem. While funding is a primary driver, the geographical dimension in an archipelago nation remains a critical, under-researched variable. Objective: This study aims to analyze the influence of Funding on the Fintech SCF Ecosystem and examine the mediating role of Geography in this relationship. Methods: This research employs a mixed-method approach. The quantitative phase utilizes Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) to analyze data from SCF investors. The qualitative phase employs Social Network Analysis (SNA) to map the relationships among ecosystem actors. Results: Quantitative results indicate that Funding has a significant positive effect on the SCF Ecosystem (t-statistic 2.938). Crucially, Geography significantly mediates this relationship (t-statistic 2.269), suggesting that funding effectiveness relies on spatial distribution. SNA results visualize the central role of platforms in bridging geographical gaps between issuers and investors. Conclusion: A robust SCF ecosystem depends not only on capital volume but on how funding strategies address geographical disparities. This study integrates the functional area of funding with geographical disparity theories within the Fintech Ecosystem framework, offering a novel perspective on "hyper-local" strategies for national inclusivity.

title: Blockchain Digital Assets, Intellectual Capital Efficiency, and Firm Performance: The Moderating Role of Ownership Concentration in Blockchain-Adopting Firms
summary: The increasing adoption of blockchain technologies raises scholars’ and managers’ concerns over how digital resources, intellectual capital and corporate governance jointly affect firm performance. However, there has been conflicting evidence on blockchain adoption’s performance implications, while studies on intellectual capital efficiency and ownership concentration are either scattered or context-specific. Furthermore, existing research rarely investigates these factors together, leaving little knowledge about their combined effects on firm performance. To fill this gap, we examine the association of blockchain digital assets and the Value-Added Intellectual Coefficient (VAIC™) with firm performance, and we explore the potential moderating role of one corporate governance characteristic, ownership concentration. Drawing on Agency Theory and the Resource-Based View and Transaction Cost Theory, the study examines whether blockchain digital assets are associated with firm performance. The prior literature suggests that blockchain may enhance organizational efficiency and reduce information asymmetry; however, these mechanisms are not directly tested in the present study. The study also treats intellectual capital as a strategic organizational asset whose contribution to firm performance may be strengthened or constrained by governance mechanisms such as ownership concentration. Using a panel of 94 blockchain-adopting public firms from various industries over 2013–2022, the study employs the System Generalized Method of Moments (SGMM) to control for endogeneity, unobserved heterogeneity and the dynamic nature of firm performance. The results indicate that blockchain digital assets are positively associated with firm performance. This association is most robust for market-based performance (Tobin’s Q); the association with accounting-based performance (Return on Assets, ROA, and Return on Equity, ROE) is weaker and sensitive to the choice of instruments and to industry and country effects. The direct effect of VAIC™ is generally insignificant and inconsistent across the estimated models. Ownership concentration does not strengthen the relationship between firm performance and blockchain digital assets. However, in the main specification, it is positive and strengthens the relationship between intellectual capital efficiency and accounting-based firm performance: the interaction between VAIC™ and ownership concentration is positive and significant for ROA and ROE, although this result is not confirmed in models with a reduced number of instruments. There is no such effect in the relationship between intellectual capital and Tobin’s Q. The study contributes to the literature a framework that integrates blockchain digital assets, intellectual capital efficiency and ownership concentration. It expands on Agency Theory by examining whether the observed relationships are consistent with theoretical arguments concerning information asymmetry, enriches the Resource-Based View by conceptualizing blockchain digital assets as strategic resources, and relates the findings to Transaction Cost Theory. However, the underlying mechanisms are not directly examined. In practice, these findings can guide managers, investors and policymakers in aligning digital transformation, intellectual capital and governance for improved firm performance.

title: The Geopolitics of Structural IP Exfiltration: Cross-Border Legal Arbitrage, Physical-Layer "Project Panama," and the Exploitation of the Japanese Knowledge Commons in Generative AI Supply Chains
summary: ■ Abstract(英文概要) This academic monograph examines the systemic, cross-border extraction of copyrighted human knowledge from non-Western jurisdictions to fuel Frontier Generative AI models. Focusing on the joint supply chain operations between US AI developer Anthropic, PBC, Japanese distribution conglomerate Nippon Shuppan Hanbai (Nippan IPS), and platform ecosystem giant Rakuten Group, this paper analyzes the material, legal, and economic mechanisms that enable large-scale intellectual property exfiltration. Specifically, we investigate court disclosures from Bartz v. Anthropic, which reveal "Project Panama"—a physical-layer procurement scheme involving the export of over 50 metric tons (~100,000 physical volumes) of Japanese copyrighted books to scanning centers in North America. By leveraging the technical translation infrastructure of "Nippan Loader" (which maps Japanese NDC/C-code metadata to US BISAC taxonomies), Anthropic obtained pristine, human-authored Japanese training corpora to bypass synthetic data degradation and AI "slop." We dissect how this apparatus operates via cross-border legal arbitrage: exploiting the Exhaustion Principle under Article 26-2 of the Japanese Copyright Act for physical exports, alongside the First-Sale Doctrine and Fair Use under US Copyright Law (§107) for destructive optical scanning. Furthermore, this study details how Japanese creators were structurally excluded from the $1.5 billion Bartz v. Anthropic class action settlement due to formal US Copyright Office registration prerequisites. Finally, we formulate three mandatory counter-strategies—physical provenance tracking, anti-digitization resale covenants, and institutional licensing models—to restore economic sustainability to the global knowledge commons.

title: Strengthening accounting practice through school-community partnerships: Bridging theory and practice in accounting education
summary: The persistent theory-practice gap in accounting education raises concerns about graduates’ preparedness for professional practice. This study proposes and examines a model explaining how school-community partnerships can bridge this gap and improve accounting graduate outcomes. Drawing on experiential learning, situated learning, stakeholder, and communities of practice theories, the model illustrates how institutional support and community engagement shape partnership activities between educational institutions and external stakeholders. These partnerships are expected to connect classroom learning with professional practice by facilitating knowledge transfer, experiential learning, professional socialization, digital competence, and workplace readiness. The model further explains how these learning mechanisms contribute to graduate outcomes, highlighting the pathways through which collaboration can translate into improved professional preparedness. Using survey data from 302 stakeholders across Ghanaian institutions, the study examines the relationships represented in the model. The findings provide support for several proposed relationships, particularly the roles of institutional support and community engagement in fostering partnerships, and the contributions of knowledge transfer, professional socialization, digital competence, and workplace readiness to graduate outcomes. The study offers an educational framework for designing accounting curricula that integrate academic instruction with authentic professional experiences. It also highlights the importance of coordinated engagement among universities, employers, accounting firms, and professional bodies in developing graduates equipped with the practical, technological, and professional competencies required by the evolving accounting profession.

title: Linking intention, readiness, and AI adoption: a configurational and capability-based perspective from accounting professionals in Syria
summary: This study examines artificial intelligence (AI) adoption among accounting professionals in Syria by integrating the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2) with AI readiness. Using survey data from 408 accounting professionals, the study applies partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA). The results show that performance expectancy, facilitating conditions, hedonic motivation, and habit significantly influence behavioral intention, whereas effort expectancy and social influence do not. Behavioral intention is positively associated with AI readiness and AI adoption behavior. AI readiness also positively influences adoption behavior and demonstrates a significant indirect effect in the intention–adoption relationship. The fsQCA results reveal multiple sufficient configurations, highlighting equifinality and configurational asymmetry and indicating that AI adoption depends on combinations of motivational and capability-related conditions rather than individual predictors. The findings suggest that accounting firms and policymakers should strengthen AI literacy, professional training, digital infrastructure, data governance, and organizational support. The study extends UTAUT2 by incorporating AI readiness as a capability-related mechanism and provides context-sensitive evidence from Syria’s underexplored institutional environment.

title: The Effect of Outstanding Loan, Non-Performing Loan, and Loan Growth on Fintech P2P Lending Profitability
summary: Introduction/Main Objectives: This study aims to analyze the effect of Outstanding Loans, Non-Performing Loans, and Loan Growth on profitability in the Fintech Peer-to-Peer (P2P) Lending industry in Indonesia. The fintech P2P lending industry in Indonesia has grown rapidly, but profitability performance has shown instability despite increasing loan disbursement, indicating an imbalance between loan growth and credit quality. Novelty: This research offers originality through the use of monthly aggregate data from the Indonesian fintech P2P lending industry, analyzed within both short-term and long-term frameworks using the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) approach, providing a more comprehensive understanding of the dynamics of financing, credit quality, and profitability. Research Methods: This study employs a quantitative approach using 36 monthly aggregate time-series observations from January 2022 to December 2024, obtained from the Fintech Lending Statistics Report published by the Financial Services Authority (OJK). The analysis utilizes the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) model to examine both short-run and long-run relationships among the variables. Finding/Results: The results indicate that in the short run, Outstanding Loans have a negative and significant effect only at lag 3, while Non-Performing Loans and Loan Growth show no significant effects. In the long run, Outstanding Loans and Non-Performing Loans have negative and significant effects on profitability, whereas Loan Growth has a positive but insignificant effect. Conclusion: Profitability depends more on effective loan management and credit quality than on loan growth alone, making sound credit risk management essential for sustainability.

title: Does artificial intelligence improve social stability risk performance in China?
summary: This paper examines whether and how artificial intelligence (AI) contributes to improving the social stability risk level in China. Against the backdrop of rapid digital transformation and increasingly complex governance challenges, AI has been widely adopted in areas such as public security, social management, and risk monitoring. However, its actual effectiveness in mitigating social stability risks remains underexplored. Drawing on panel data from multiple regions in China, this study constructs an empirical framework to evaluate the impact of AI policy on social stability risk levels. The analysis integrates indicators of technological capacity, governance performance, and socio-economic conditions, and applies quantitative methods to identify both direct and indirect effects. The findings suggest that AI policy significantly reduces social stability risks by promoting digital economy development, increasing wage levels and investment in education. At the same time, the results reveal notable regional heterogeneity. The AI policy significantly reduces social stability risk in the central and western regions, and areas with moderate digital economy development, but has no statistically significant effect in economically developed and digitally advanced areas. The study also highlights potential challenges, including data governance concerns and uneven technological access, which may offset some of AI's benefits. This research contributes to the literature by linking technological innovation with social governance outcomes and provides policy implications for leveraging AI to promote social stability. It suggests that policymakers should not only invest in AI infrastructure but also address institutional and regional disparities to ensure inclusive and effective risk management.

title: Digital Infrastructure Access, Fintech Adoption, And Financial Inclusion Among Smallholder Farmers in North Central Nigeria: A PLS-SEM Analysis
summary: Purpose: Smallholder farmers account for the majority of Nigeria's food production yet remain largely excluded from formal financial services, constraining productivity and rural economic development. This study examines whether access to digital infrastructure drives FinTech adoption among smallholder farmers, and whether FinTech adoption, in turn, translates into meaningful financial inclusion. Design/Methodology/Approach: A quantitative, cross-sectional survey design was employed. Structured questionnaires were administered face-to-face to smallholder farmers across Benue, Nasarawa, Plateau, and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Abuja in Nigeria's North Central region, using a stratified multi-stage sampling procedure. Of 445 questionnaires distributed, 392 valid responses were obtained (88.1% response rate). Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS was used to assess the measurement model and to test the hypothesised structural relationships between digital infrastructure access, FinTech adoption, and financial inclusion. Findings: All constructs demonstrated strong reliability and convergent validity (Cronbach's alpha, composite reliability, and AVE values exceeding recommended thresholds). Digital infrastructure access exerted a strong, positive, and statistically significant effect on FinTech adoption (β = 0.934, t = 138.009, p < 0.001), explaining 87.2% of the variance in adoption. FinTech adoption, in turn, had a strong positive effect on financial inclusion (β = 0.873, t = 50.832, p < 0.001). Both hypothesised paths were robustly supported, with effect sizes considerably larger than those typically reported in comparable technology-adoption studies. Practical Implications: The findings indicate that digital infrastructure functions as a threshold precondition rather than a marginal enabler of FinTech adoption in resource constrained rural settings. Policymakers, mobile network operators, and FinTech providers should therefore prioritise rural connectivity and infrastructure investment as a precondition for financial-inclusion programming, rather than treating infrastructure and adoption facilitation initiatives as parallel, independent workstreams. Originality: This study provides rare, statistically robust, empirically grounded evidence of the infrastructure–adoption–inclusion pathway among smallholder farmers in a developing economy agricultural setting, using a large, regionally stratified sample and rigorous PLS SEM validation. It extends Rogers' Diffusion of Innovation theory by demonstrating that communication-channel access can function as a binding constraint rather than a merely facilitating condition in infrastructure-scarce rural economies.

title: The Adoption of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Features in Property Valuation in Ibadan, Oyo State, Nigeria
summary: The growing emphasis on sustainability and long-term value creation has increased the relevance of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) features in property valuation. However, there is limited and inconsistent adoption of ESG features in property valuation practice in the emerging market context. This paper evaluates the drivers of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) features integration in valuation practice of properties in Ibadan, Oyo State, Nigeria. Out of the 190 Estate Surveying and Valuation firms in the 2024 Nigerian Institution of Estate Surveyors and Valuers (NIESV) Directory, valid surveys from 179 respondent firms were completed, representing 94.2% retrieval rate. The analysis utilized descriptive statistics, the Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin (KMO) and Bartlett’s tests, principal component analysis with Varimax rotation, and composite factor scoring. Three latent factors (comprising 78.13% of the variance) were revealed: External Drivers (composite mean = 4.19), Internal Capabilities (composite mean = 3.89), and Economic Constraints (composite mean = 3.81). External Drivers were comprised of Government Regulations, client demand, and lack of awareness. Internal Capabilities included data availability, competitive advantage, and compliance with international standards. Economic Constraints were dominated by high implementation costs. External regulatory and market forces have the greatest influence. The current study supports the need to develop internal capacity and address cost barriers, as these are expected to facilitate continuous adoption. The following recommendations were made: introduction of mandated ESG reporting standards, accredited continuing professional development, and the staggered adoption of guidelines.

title: Commerce Core Expansion: Auditing Small-Model Adaptation for Product Matching and Attribute Extraction
summary: Small language models could support several product-understanding operations within a retailer’s infrastructure, but evidence of task accuracy is easily con-founded with evidence of generalization or serving efficiency. We study QLoRA adaptation of Qwen3-1.7B for query–product relevance, listing identity, functional relation, technical compatibility, and brand/color extraction. We reconstruct the experiments from committed data, checkpoint histories, training logs, prediction records, and serving traces, and release an offline audit that regenerates the quanti-tative analysis. On a common 200-listing extraction sample, the dedicated adapter attains brand F1 of 1.000 and color F1 of 0.955 under the recorded permissive matching rule; the latter exceeds the strongest tested API comparator by 1.38 per-centage points. This is a descriptive result: two evaluation texts also occur in training, and missing paired outputs prevent a significance claim. Matching re-sults expose a different problem. Adapter and API relevance scores use different samples; a single-token relevance adapter reaches 0.5115 accuracy but only 0.436 macro-F1; and 25 of 28 functional-relation test rows reuse training scenarios. A checkpoint sweep further exposes that test partition to model selection. We for-malize the information required for comparable evaluations, demonstrate scorer counterexamples, and bound the paired correctness uncertainty recoverable from aggregate extraction counts. Historical load tests contain no completed inference requests. A separate RunPod follow-up adds paired development evaluations un-der two prompt interfaces, a text-extraction comparator and bounded HTTP serv-ing measurements; these do not establish final-test generalization or production cost advantage. The evidence supports promising narrow extraction behavior and a reproducible account of evaluation failure modes, rather than universal superior-ity or a production-ready horizontal model.

title: ESG performance and firm performance: The mediating role of green technology innovation disclosure in Indonesian Firms
summary: Abstract The increasing necessities of sustainable development has driven attention towards the relationship between Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) and firm financial performance, specifically for environmentally sensitive sectors. The available empirical results are still limited, and very few studies particularly examine whether Green Technology Innovation Disclosure (GTID) can act as a mediator between ESG and firm performance in emerging markets. This research attempts to examine the relationship between ESG and firm performance while testing the mediating role of GTID on energy and industrial companies listed on Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX). Using a balanced panel data set of 82 companies over 4 years (2021-2024) with total 328 observations, by employing fixed-effects panel regression and the Generalized Structural Equation Modeling (GSEM) with 5,000 bootstrap replications estimate the indirect effect. The result indicated Insufficient evidence of a positive association between ESG and return on assets (ROA) that statistically significant at 10 percent. However, this relationship is sensitive to alternative specifications, as the ESG coefficient becomes statistically insignificant when return on equity (ROE) is used and is statistically significant only around the median of the conditional ROA distribution. More importantly, ESG performance is not significantly associated with GTID, GTID is not significantly associated with ROA, and the bootstrapped indirect effect is statistically insignificant. Thus, the findings do not support GTID as a mediating mechanism between ESG performance and firm performance. The study highlights the importance of distinguishing disclosure-based green technology measures from the substantive implementation and economic intensity of actual green technological innovation when evaluating their financial implications.

title: Integrasi Faktor Lingkungan, Sosial, dan Tata Kelola (ESG) dalam Manajemen Keuangan Perusahaan
summary: Integrasi faktor Lingkungan, Sosial, dan Tata Kelola (ESG) dalam manajemen keuangan perusahaan semakin dianggap sebagai elemen penting dalam perencanaan dan pengambilan keputusan finansial yang berkelanjutan. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis bagaimana perusahaan mengintegrasikan prinsip-prinsip ESG dalam manajemen keuangan mereka dan mengeksplorasi dampak penerapan ESG terhadap kinerja keuangan perusahaan. Dengan menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif berbasis studi kasus dan analisis konten, penelitian ini mengumpulkan data primer melalui wawancara mendalam dengan pengambil keputusan di sektor keuangan dan keberlanjutan, serta data sekunder dari laporan tahunan dan laporan keberlanjutan perusahaan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa faktor lingkungan, sosial, dan tata kelola secara signifikan mempengaruhi keputusan investasi, alokasi modal, serta pengelolaan risiko dalam perusahaan. Integrasi ESG memungkinkan perusahaan untuk mengurangi risiko jangka panjang terkait dengan perubahan regulasi lingkungan, konflik sosial, dan praktik tata kelola yang buruk. Selain itu, perusahaan yang mengimplementasikan kebijakan ESG yang kuat menunjukkan peningkatan efisiensi operasional dan dapat memperoleh akses yang lebih baik ke modal, meningkatkan reputasi, dan mengurangi biaya modal. Meskipun demikian, tantangan utama yang dihadapi adalah kurangnya standar konsisten dalam pengukuran dan pelaporan kinerja ESG, serta kesulitan dalam mengukur dampak langsung dari faktor ESG terhadap kinerja finansial jangka pendek. Penelitian ini memberikan wawasan mengenai pentingnya integrasi ESG dalam manajemen keuangan untuk menciptakan nilai jangka panjang yang berkelanjutan dan mengurangi ketidakpastian di pasar global.

title: Preference ≠ Tattooability: Auditing Reward Models for AI Tattoo Generation
summary: AI tattoo generation is usually ranked with the same reward models that rank general text-to-image outputs. Those models predict which image a crowd annotator prefers. A tattoo that will be worn also has to survive a needle, a gap that heals shut, and ink that spreads. We audited that gap with deterministic, physically scaled probes and with CLIPScore, PickScore, HPSv2.1 and ImageReward, on tattoo-subject pairs from HPDv2 and ImageRewardDB, on controlled defects, and on a print-scale ink-spread stress test. On HPDv2 tattoo-subject pairs, a-priori probes agree with human preference below chance, and that contrast remains after a Holm correction across scorers. Nothing here ranks a commercial AI tattoo generator. Competing interest: the author operates tatany.app; that product was not evaluated or ranked.
